The completion $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ of $\Cl(p,q)$ carries the null pair $
O = 	frac12(e_{-} - e_{+})$, $
Inf = e_{-} + e_{+}$ with $
O \cdot 
Inf = -1$, and represents the point $x$ by the null vector $X(x) = 
O + x + 	frac12 Q(x)
Inf$, with $X(x)\cdot X(y) = -	frac12 Q(x - y)$. For a null vector $v$ and $u$ orthogonal to it, $R_{u} = 1 + vu$ is a rotor fixing $v$; and for a null partner $w$ of $v$ ($v \cdot w 
eq 0$) and $U = \{v, w\}^{\perp}$, the nondegenerate complement of the hyperbolic plane they span, $u \mapsto R_{u}$ (for $u \in U$) is an isomorphism of $(U, +)$ onto the group of null rotations of $v$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Sec.~4.3, Lem.~4.6, Thm.~4.10]{ButlerT1}.
angle.imported-conformal-model-null-rota.technical:
The completion $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ of $\Cl(p,q)$ adjoins a null pair $
O = 	frac12(e_{-} - e_{+})$, $
Inf = e_{-} + e_{+}$ with $
O\cdot
Inf = -1$. A point $x$ is represented by the null vector $X(x) = 
O + x + 	frac12 Q(x)
Inf$, and the inner product of two representatives encodes their squared separation: $X(x)\cdot X(y) = -	frac12 Q(x-y)$.

For a null vector $v$ and $u$ orthogonal to it, $R_u = 1 + vu$ is a rotor fixing $v$; and for a null partner $w$ of $v$ ($v \cdot w 
eq 0$) and $U = \{v, w\}^{\perp}$, $u \mapsto R_u$ (for $u \in U$) is an isomorphism of the additive group $(U,+)$ onto the group of null rotations of $v$. Both facts are carried over from earlier in the series.
angle.imported-conformal-model-null-rota.lay: Adding two extra directions to the algebra of space lets every point be written as a null vector, one whose square is zero, and the squared distance between two points can then be read off from a simple product of their vectors. In the same setting, each null direction has a family of rotations that leave it fixed, and these rotations combine exactly like ordinary addition of vectors. Both facts are carried over from earlier work in the series.

correspondence.chevalley-pairing.technical:
On the Fock module $\Lambda^\bullet W$ let $\alpha$ act on $\Lambda^k W$ by $(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$ and let $\operatorname{top}$ take the coefficient of the top form $w_1\wedge w_2\wedge w_3$; the Chevalley pairing is $B(x,y) = \operatorname{top}(\alpha(x)\wedge y)$. It vanishes on $\CS\times\CS$ and on $\CSm\times\CSm$, restricts to a perfect pairing between $\CS$ and $\CSm$, and is antisymmetric, $B(y,x) = -B(x,y)$.

Every vector is self-transpose, $B(c(v)x, y) = B(x, c(v)y)$ for $v \in V_\C$, and each bivector $\beta_{uv} = \tfrac12 c(u)c(v)$ with $\ip{u}{v} = 0$ is skew, $B(\beta_{uv}x, y) + B(x, \beta_{uv}y) = 0$: the pairing is infinitesimally $\Spin$-invariant.
correspondence.chevalley-pairing.lay: The spinor space of the completion carries a natural way, due to Chevalley, of pairing two spinors to give a number. This result fixes all its signs: it pairs the two chirality halves with each other, it changes sign when the two inputs are swapped, and it is compatible with the action of vectors and of the infinitesimal symmetries.
correspondence.chevalley-pairing.typing_note: No edges; the pairing is classical (Chevalley) but no imported claim for it is in the store, so no standard route.

proofs.main:
(1) $B(x,y)$ can be nonzero only when $\deg x + \deg y = 3$, which is odd; two elements of the same parity pair to zero. Perfection between $\CS$ (degrees $0,2$) and $\CSm$ (degrees $3,1$): on the monomial bases, $B(1, w_{123}) = 1$, $B(w_{23}, w_1) = \alpha(w_{23})\wedge w_1$-coefficient $= -\operatorname{top}(w_2\wedge w_3\wedge w_1) = -1$, and cyclically; the Gram matrix of $B$ between the two four-dimensional halves is a signed permutation matrix, hence invertible (the script checks that it has rank four).
(2) For $x \in \Lambda^k$, $y \in \Lambda^{3-k}$: $B(y,x) = (-1)^{(3-k)(2-k)/2}\operatorname{top}(y \wedge x)$ and $y\wedge x = (-1)^{k(3-k)}x\wedge y$, so $B(y,x)/B(x,y) = (-1)^{(3-k)(2-k)/2 + k(3-k) - k(k-1)/2}$; evaluating the exponent at $k = 0,1,2,3$ gives $3, 3, 1, -3$, odd in every degree, so the ratio is $-1$ throughout.
(3) For $w \in W$ (wedge case): $\alpha(w \wedge x)\wedge y = (-1)^{k(k+1)/2}\,w\wedge x\wedge y$ while $\alpha(x)\wedge(w\wedge y) = (-1)^{k(k-1)/2}(-1)^k\,w\wedge x\wedge y$; the two sign prefactors agree, since $k(k+1)/2 - k(k-1)/2 - k = 0$. For $w' \in W'$ (contraction case): when $\deg x + \deg y = 4$ the form $\alpha(x)\wedge y$ vanishes (degree exceeds three), so applying the graded Leibniz rule for $\iota_{w'}$ to it gives $0 = \iota_{w'}(\alpha(x))\wedge y + (-1)^k \alpha(x)\wedge \iota_{w'}(y)$, i.e.\ $\iota_{w'}(x)\wedge y = (-1)^{k+1} x \wedge \iota_{w'}(y)$ after dividing by $(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$. Taking $\operatorname{top}$ and restoring the $\alpha$-prefactors of the two sides ($(-1)^{(k-1)(k-2)/2}$ on the left, $(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$ on the right, whose ratio is $(-1)^{k-1}$) yields $B(\iota_{w'}x, y) = (-1)^{k+1}(-1)^{k-1} B(x, \iota_{w'}y) = B(x, \iota_{w'}y)$. Both cases scale by the common $\sqrt2$.
(4) By (3), $B(c(u)c(v)x, y) = B(x, c(v)c(u)y)$, and $c(v)c(u) = -c(u)c(v) + 2\ip{u}{v} = -c(u)c(v)$ for orthogonal $u, v$. The verification script checks (1) to (4) on the full basis in exact arithmetic.

__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-chevalley-pa: The passage from the module $\Lambda^\bullet W$ back to the vector space $V_\C$ is a bilinear pairing on spinors that Chevalley's construction carries with it \cite{Chevalley54}. We set it out with every sign computed, since the signs are what the incidence theorem depends on. Fix a generator $w_1 \wedge w_2 \wedge w_3$ of the line $\Lambda^3 W$ and write $\operatorname{top}(\xi)$ for the coefficient of $w_1\wedge w_2\wedge w_3$ in the degree-three component of $\xi \in \Lambda^\bullet W$. Let $\alpha$ be the linear map acting on $\Lambda^k W$ as $(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$, so $\alpha = +1$ on degrees $0, 1$ and $-1$ on degrees $2, 3$. Throughout, $\mathrm{Spin}(V_\C)$ denotes the group generated by the exponentials of all bivectors $\beta \in \Lambda^2 V_\C$, realised in the Clifford algebra as $\tfrac12 c(u)c(v)$ for orthogonal $u, v$ and their sums, acting on vectors by conjugation ($e^{\beta} c(v) e^{-\beta} = c(e^{\operatorname{ad}\beta} v)$, the vector action being computed in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}) and on the module by the given action; $\rho$ denotes the action of bivectors on $\Lambda^\bullet W$ and on its halves, $\rho(u\wedge v) := \tfrac12 c(u)c(v) - \tfrac12\ip{u}{v}$ (Propositions \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation} and \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}).
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-what-proved-:
\emph{Proved in this paper, at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1}:} the Fock model theorem and the chirality split (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}); the Chevalley pairing with its four sign clauses (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chevalley-pairing}); the spinor identification $V_\C \cong \Lambda^2\T$ with the norm correspondence and the Klein-quadric clause (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}); the skew-lines/splitting/hyperbolic-plane equivalence (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}); the incidence theorem with the term-by-term chart identification and coverage (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}); the reality proposition: the conjugation, the Hermitian twistor form, the $\Sigma$-nullity of real incidence lines, the $(2,2)$ signature and the factor $i$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}); the chiral planes and the summand spaces (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}); the three-language dictionary (Corollary \claimref{correspondence.one-statement-three-languages}); the tractor-connection decomposition and the local twistor identification up to the one imported convention of Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification} (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}); the statistics no-go (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.statistics-no-go}); the spin representation isomorphism (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}); the purity and Fock-vacuum theorem (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}); the palatial quadratic algebra, the Clifford ordering shift, and the shared-core theorem (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}, Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}); the Lorentzian duality lemma and the half-flat no-go (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat}); the ordering filtration and the ASD ordering insensitivity (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.ordering-filtration}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}).

\emph{Imported as Facts with provenance:} the forced completion and the real ladder results (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-forced-completion-fibre-quadric}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}); the flat-model stabilisers (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}); the vacuum/scale-tractor equivalences (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations-scale-tractor}); the tractor connection and the classical local twistor formula (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}); the nonlinear graviton (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton}); the Weyl-star commutation (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-weyl-commutes-duality}); Weyl's theorem (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem}); complete reducibility for $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-complete-reducibility}); the sign convention relating Penrose and Rindler's $\mathrm{P}_{ab}$ to the Schouten tensor (Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification}).

\emph{Conjectural, and declared as such:} the googly localisation (Conjecture \claimref{correspondence.googly-localisation-quartic-order}), whose ordering-insensitivity consistency conditions are proved (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}) and whose analytic half is open.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-machine-veri:
Every computational identity asserted in this paper is verified by the deposited script \texttt{verify\_T09.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT9}, which imports the series' shared exact-arithmetic library \texttt{GA.py} and runs entirely in exact arithmetic over the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$: no floating point appears anywhere, so every check is an identity, not an approximation. The script works with $C(v) = c(v)/\sqrt2$ (the section “Setting and imports”), so that $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$ and $C(u)^2 = Q(u)/2$, and with the isotropic basis of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}, which is Gaussian rational. Sixty-nine checks pass. Three reusable routines developed for this paper were promoted into \texttt{GA.py} per the series' practice, append-only and backward compatibly: an exact Gaussian-rational field class, generic-field linear algebra (rank, solve) usable over any exact field, and a kernel routine over any exact field.

The coverage, by section. \emph{The Fock model} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}): the CAR relations of the three wedge and contraction pairs $w_j\wedge$, $\iota_{w_j'}$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}, there written $A_1$, $B_1$) and all anticommutators on the full state basis; $\{C(u), C(v)\} = \ip{u}{v}$ on all thirty-six basis pairs and $C(u)^2 = Q(u)/2$ on non-null, complex, and null instances; linear independence of the sixty-four ordered generator products in $\End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$ (rank $64$: simplicity, surjectivity and irreducibility at once); oddness of vectors; the even subalgebra of dimension exactly $32$. \emph{The Chevalley pairing} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chevalley-pairing}): parity vanishing, perfection of the $\T'\times\T$ block, antisymmetry on all sixty-four pairs, $B$-self-transposedness of all six basis vectors, and invariance under all fifteen antisymmetrised bivectors. \emph{The spinor identification} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, Example \claimref{note.correspondence.isomorphism-witt-pair}): antisymmetry of $G_v$; rank six of $\Psi$; the norm correspondence on all twenty-one pairs with the computed constant ($-1$ for the $C$-normalised $\Psi$, i.e.\ $-2$ in the paper's normalisation); the exact values $\Psi_C(w_1) = -t_2\wedge t_3$, $\Psi_C(w_1') = t_0 \wedge t_1$ and their planes; the Pfaffian nullity criterion on null and non-null instances; equivariance $\Psi(\beta v) = \beta\cdot\Psi(v)$ for all fifteen bivectors on all six basis vectors (ninety identities). \emph{Incidence} (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}, Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}): the hyperbolic pair; the expansion, norm identity, chart identification $P(A) = X(m(A))$ and simplicity for four sample maps $A$ (identity, Gaussian-rational, singular, and $i$ times a Hermitian matrix); the sign flip $-2\det(i\hat x) = +2\det\hat x$ on a sample map; the coverage pairing. \emph{Reality} (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}): the real orthonormal basis and its relation to the isotropic one; the conjugation as the reflection in $b_4$ composed with coordinate conjugation; $\kappa\,C(v) = C(\bar v)\,\kappa$ on every basis state for the six basis vectors and their $i$-multiples; $\kappa^2 = -\tfrac12$ (the $C$-normalised $-1$) and the parity swap; the constant $\lambda_0 = \lambda = 1$ on the full basis, and the general relation $\Sigma(Z_2,Z_1) = \lambda\,\overline{\Sigma(Z_1,Z_2)}$ with its phase repair tested on $\kappa$ rescaled by $(3+4i)/5$, where $\lambda \neq 1$; $\Sigma$ Hermitian and of rank four; $\Som$ and $\Spi$ both $\Sigma$-null; the signature $(2,2)$ read off $\Sigma$ through its real form; all fifteen real bivectors $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitian; four $\sigma$-Hermitian $\hat x$ with $m(i\hat x)$ real and spanning $W_{1,3}$, and $m(\hat x)$ not real. \emph{Chiral planes and summands} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(3)): each chirality factor annihilates exactly one of $\Som$, $\Spi$ and acts faithfully on the other, the two factors on different planes; the summand composite equals $C(e_a)C(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$, the $C$-form of $\tfrac12 c(e_a)c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$, on $\Som$ for all sixteen pairs of mixed directions. \emph{Stabilisers and local twistors} (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-shift}): the commutator identity $[\beta, C(w)] = C(\beta w)$ for all fifteen bivectors; trace-freeness and linear independence of the fifteen spinor actions (the $\mathfrak{sl}(\T)$ isomorphism); the stabiliser census $10 + 1 + 4$ of the infinity direction and the exact match with preservation of the plane $\Som$; both summand actions on all four mixed directions; the full eigenvalue table of $\rho(v\wedge v^*) = N - \tfrac12$. \emph{Twistors as states} (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}): the annihilator of the vacuum; purity (dimension three, total isotropy) of a generic even and a generic odd spinor; the joint-kernel line; generation of the whole module from a vacuum by its dual system; the CAR relations of the generic twistor's own pair system, built on its annihilator and the dual complement constructed in the proof. \emph{The palatial algebra} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}, Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}): the relations $[Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\delta$ in the realisation $\bar Z = -\hbar\,\partial$; the homogeneity identity $q(\mathrm{id}) = -(h+2)\hbar$ (the $-2s-2$ point of contact) on all monomials of degree $\le 3$; $[q(M), q(N)] = \hbar\,q([M,N])$ and the adjoint action for explicit Gaussian-rational $M, N$, checked on the determining monomial basis; the symmetric-versus-normal ordering shift. \emph{The chirality split} (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure}, Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}): the full $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ bracket table, all fifteen brackets including the three vanishing $[R_i, B_i]$; closure and mutual commutation of the two chirality factors; $\ast^2 = -1$ on all six basis $2$-forms; and the $\pm i$ eigenvector property of the chirality generators $A^{(1)}_i, A^{(2)}_i$, with conjugate eigenvalues. The script exits nonzero on any failure and prints one line per check, tagged by the statement it certifies.
__notes__.note.correspondence.what-proved-what-con: The conjecture's \emph{algebraic} half is a theorem. Quadratic ambiguities are central and carry nothing; the first tensorial slot is quartic and is $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$-valued (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.ordering-filtration}); the ASD sector closes under ordering discrepancies and never sources the googly slot (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}). These are exactly the consistency conditions clause (a) needs, and they were not automatic: they depended on the chirality split commuting, which is special to four dimensions. What remains open is the \emph{analytic} half: the palatial construction itself, i.e.\ a deformation in which clause (b)'s quartic tensor demonstrably reproduces prescribed self-dual curvature. That construction is the googly problem in palatial form and is beyond this paper; the conjecture registers the precise expectation, and Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector} is its first falsifiable check, passed.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-successor-pr: Five problems are named. (1) \emph{The analytic googly half:} construct the palatial deformation of Conjecture \claimref{correspondence.googly-localisation-quartic-order}(b), or refute the localisation; Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector} is the consistency check any construction must pass. (2) \emph{The quantised incidence relation:} promote $\omega = I_6\hat x\pi$ (Penrose's $\omega = ix\pi$) to an operator equation in $\mathcal{P}$ (the incidence line as a subspace annihilated by operator combinations of the quantised twistor), and determine what replaces the chart of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart} one storey up. (3) \emph{Local twistors over the wall:} extend Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection} across the degenerate walls of \cite{ButlerT4}, where the tractor bundle persists but the scale splitting fails; the wall sequence should act on the spin bundle by the completion's own ladder operators. (4) \emph{Massless fields:} develop the Penrose transform in the series' language. The homogeneity $-2s-2$ is stated and proved from the ordering shift of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}(4) in the spectrum paper T7 \cite[Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT7}; what remains open is the transform itself in the series' language. (5) \emph{The real-form dictionary in full:} the $\mathbb{PN}$ hypersurface as the whole real conformal compactification, the two open regions $\PT^\pm$ where $\Sigma$ is definite, and the two ruling families over the reals, completing Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor} beyond the affine chart.
__notes__.note.correspondence.dimensions-real-form: Over the reals, $\Cl(2,4) \cong \Mat_4(\HH)$ and $\Cl^0(2,4) \cong \Mat_4(\C)$; the paper never uses these classification statements as inputs (the complexified Fock model carries all the structure), but they locate the construction in the standard tables, and the counts $64 = 4^2\cdot 4$ and $32 = 4^2 \cdot 2$ are the ones that make them possible. What the real structure of $V \subset V_\C$ adds is an antilinear conjugation $\kappa$ on the module, constructed explicitly and shown unique up to scale in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}, which pairs the conformal spinor space $\CS$ with its opposite chirality $\CSm$: this is the statement that the opposite chirality is the conjugate of the conformal spinor space (dual twistors are conjugate twistors), and it induces on $\CS$ the Hermitian form of signature $(2,2)$ preserved by $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4) \cong SU(2,2)$. The signature is computed in the incidence section, where the $(\omega, \pi)$ splitting makes it a two-line count (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}(4)). \emph{Point of contact (per the series' practice):} $\CS$ with its $SU(2,2)$ structure is exactly Penrose's twistor space \cite{Penrose1967, PenroseRindler86}, and the conjugation pairing $\CS \leftrightarrow \CSm$ is his twistor-dual-twistor conjugation.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-nonlinear-gr: The correspondence proved so far is flat-model and connection-level. The question that decides whether twistor geometry can carry \emph{curved} vacuum gravity is Penrose's: which spacetimes globalise the point-line dictionary? The classical answer is exactly the half-flat sector, and this section records that answer with its Lorentzian boundary stated, then poses the series' conjecture about where the missing (googly) half lies in the palatial algebra, together with a proof of the conjecture's algebraic half.
__notes__.note.correspondence.boundary-stated-plai: Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton} and Proposition \claimref{correspondence.no-real-lorentzian-vacuum-half-flat} together are the boundary of the correspondence: the nonlinear graviton globalises the completion's point space in the Euclidean and complexified sectors, where half-flatness is a nontrivial condition, and \emph{never} for a real Lorentzian black hole. Encoding the full, two-sided Einstein equations in data on the projective spinor space $\PCS$ (twistor data) is the googly problem, open in every formalism, including this one. What the transport framework does capture of the Lorentzian black hole's structure on the conformal spinor space (its twistorial nature) is the type-D structure: the Kerr conformal scale is the inverse cube of the Walker-Penrose Killing spinor \cite[Prop.~6.8]{ButlerT6}, a statement at the level of the section “Incidence encodes the completion”'s dictionary, not of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton}'s globalisation.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-position-ser:
This paper is T9 of the series. \emph{It relies on four predecessors:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} for the Clifford conventions (the section “Setting and imports”); the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the forced completion, its fibre quadric, the real ladder pairs and the transvection no-go (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-forced-completion-fibre-quadric}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}); the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the iterated ascent whose rungs are the ladder pairs of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs} (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}, Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.point-contact-planes-tower}); the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the flat-model stabilisers, the scale tractor and the vacuum equations, the tractor connection, and the Kerr Killing spinor (Facts \claimref{correspondence.imported-stabilisers-flat-model}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-vacuum-equations-scale-tractor}, \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}, Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.boundary-stated-plainly}). No result is imported from the spectrum paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7}, which is named in successor problem (4) as the paper that proves its homogeneity half from this paper's ordering shift; the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} is named in the introduction and in successor problem (3), and the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} as context.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} assigns the twistor restatement of its spectrum condition to this paper's setting; the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} cites the twistor reading of the completion's spinor module as a point of contact; the spectrum paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} imports the ordering shift of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}(4); the action paper T10 \cite{ButlerT10} imports nothing from this paper: the summand decomposition of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}(1) reappears there, in the frozen point's scale, as its own Lemma 2.5(iii), proved directly; the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the pure-spinor identification of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, the chart normalisation of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}, and the palatial quadratics of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} imports the spinor identification, the pure-spinor theorem and the shared core (Theorems \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}, \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}); the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the Witt-flag reading of the ladder pairs; the synthesis paper T16 \cite{ButlerT16} imports the point embedding and the Fock-vacuum reading; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-introduction:
The transport principle \cite{ButlerT1} resolves division by zero in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ by a forced minimal completion into $\Cl(2,4)$, and the series has so far exploited the completion's vector side: the fibre quadric whose points resolve the division \cite{ButlerT1}, the sheaf of completions over a degenerating metric \cite{ButlerT4}, the tower of iterated completions and its CAR limit \cite{ButlerT3}, the vacuum equations as a parallel ideal point of the quadric \cite{ButlerT6}, and T5's chain from the Schwarzschild gauge field to the Page curve \cite{ButlerT5}. This paper develops the completion's \emph{spinor} side, and finds there a formalism that has existed since 1967: Penrose's twistor theory.

The correspondence is not an analogy, and the paper's task is to prove it as a set of theorems and then apply it in both directions. In one direction, the series gains: fifty years of twistor technology (the Klein correspondence, the incidence geometry, local twistor transport, the twistor description of massless fields) becomes available to the transport programme with an explicit dictionary. In the other direction, the series contributes: the completion explains \emph{why} the twistorial objects are what they are. The two distinguished skew lines of projective twistor space are the null pair adjoined by the Witt completion; the incidence relation is the completion's chart, re-derived rather than postulated; and the palatial programme's noncommutative twistor algebra is exactly one quantisation above the completion's ladder pairs, with the conformal algebra as the shared core.

Three questions organise the paper. \emph{What is twistor space, from the algebra alone?} the section “Twistors as ascended spinors” answers with the Chevalley pure-spinor construction, proved outright at this dimension: the complexified ascended algebra acts irreducibly on the eight-dimensional fermionic Fock space of three null pairs, twistor space and its conjugate dual are the two chirality halves, and the ambient vector space is recovered as $\Lambda^2\T$ with the Klein quadric as its projectivised null cone (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.spinor-identification}). \emph{Where is the completion, inside twistor geometry?} the section “Incidence encodes the completion” computes the Pl\"ucker image of Penrose's incidence relation and finds, term by term, the completion's point embedding: the $(\omega,\pi)$ splitting is the Witt completion at spinor level, and the stabiliser of the infinity line is the Poincar\'e parabolic (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}); local twistor transport is then identified as the spinor square root of the tractor connection of \cite{ButlerT6}, up to one declared sign convention (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}, Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification}). \emph{What is the relation to quantised twistors?} the section “The palatial relation: two quantisations, one core” first refutes: the palatial algebra is bosonic and admits no finite-dimensional representation, so it cannot be the completion's fermionic pair algebra (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.statistics-no-go}). The corrected picture is a two-storey construction: the completion's fermionic quantisation turns ambient directions into twistor \emph{states}; the palatial bosonic quantisation turns twistor states into operators; $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ is the invariant core of both storeys, and the ordering shift of a half per dimension recurs at each (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}). the section “The nonlinear graviton, the boundary, and the googly conjecture” states the Lorentzian boundary (no real Lorentzian vacuum is half-flat) and poses the googly-at-quartic-order conjecture precisely.
__notes__.note.correspondence.point-contact-what-b: Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection} completes the identification begun in \cite{ButlerT6}: the ambient bundle of the completion is the standard conformal tractor bundle, and its spin bundle, with the induced connection, is the classical local twistor bundle, up to the one sign convention of Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.one-imported-convention-local-twistor-identification}. The series' chain of results is thus: division fails (type N) $\Rightarrow$ ascent to $\Cl(2,4)$ forced \cite{ButlerT1} $\Rightarrow$ vacuum equations are formulated in the completion as a parallel ideal point \cite{ButlerT6} $\Rightarrow$ the spinors of the completion are the conformal spinors (Penrose's twistors), and the parallel ideal point is the constant simple infinity bivector of $\CS$ (the infinity twistor) (Corollary \claimref{correspondence.one-statement-three-languages}). Each formalism was invented independently (tractors: Thomas, Bailey-Eastwood-Gover; twistors: Penrose); the completion derives both from one division problem.

The remaining step, that Penrose's composite $-\varepsilon_A{}^B\mathrm{P}_{CC'DA'}\omega^D$ equals $\tfrac12 c(e_a)c(\mathrm{P}(e_c))$ under Levi-equivariant identifications, is the statement that the tensor written $\mathrm{P}_{ab}$ in \cite{PenroseRindler86} (there $\Phi_{ab} - \Lambda g_{ab}$) is the Schouten tensor of Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-tractor-connection-local-twistor-transport}(i) with a definite sign fixed by their curvature conventions. __notes__.note.correspondence.what-factor-i-what-r: The factor $I_6$ in $\omega = I_6\hat x\pi$ (Penrose's $i$ in $\omega = ix\pi$), the complex unit of $\CS$, is thus derived: it is the anti-Hermiticity that reality of the chart point forces on the map $A$ relative to the invariant Hermitian form $\Sigma$, and it can be moved but not removed (a phase change of $\kappa$ rotates $\Sigma$ and $\hat x$ together). __notes__.note.correspondence.two-storey-picture: The corrected relationship is a proved structure, drawn in a figure of the original. The Clifford (fermionic) quantisation turns ambient directions into conformal spinor (twistor) \emph{states}: first quantisation, forced at the singular locus (Remark \claimref{note.correspondence.point-contact-planes-tower}). The Weyl (bosonic) quantisation of the palatial programme turns conformal spinor states into the noncommutative algebra of quantised conformal spinors: second quantisation, one storey up, and provably not the first storey under another name (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.statistics-no-go}). The conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ is the invariant core of both storeys (Theorem \claimref{correspondence.shared-core-ordering-dictionary}), and the ordering shift of a half per dimension recurs at each. What survives of the naive conjecture is its corrected form: the framework's operator-valued completion and Penrose's noncommutative holomorphic geometry are opposite ends of one tower rather than of one identification, meeting at the conformal algebra. Read against the tower paper \cite{ButlerT3}, the completion's ladder pairs supply the states on which the palatial storey acts.

__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-palatial-rel:
Palatial twistor theory \cite{Penrose15} is Penrose's current approach to the full Einstein equations: it replaces holomorphic functions on twistor space by a \emph{noncommutative} algebra of twistor operators, with $\bar Z$ realised as a derivative and the googly data expected to reside in ordering ambiguities. The transport framework independently produces noncommutative pair structure, the completed ladder pairs with their CAR relations, as the mandatory replacement for classical values at the singular locus \cite{ButlerT1}. It is natural to conjecture that the two structures are the same object. This section proves that the naive form of that conjecture is \emph{false}, for a reason of statistics that admits a one-line proof, and then proves the corrected picture: the two algebras are the two storeys of one tower, meeting at the conformal algebra.

Throughout, the \emph{palatial algebra} $\mathcal{P}$ is the unital associative $\C$-algebra with generators $Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta$ ($\alpha, \beta = 1, \dots, 4$) and relations
\[
[Z^\alpha, Z^\beta] = 0, \qquad [\bar Z_\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = 0, \qquad [Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\,\delta^\alpha_\beta ,
\]
the twistor canonical commutation relations of \cite{Penrose15} (there realised by $\bar Z_\beta = \hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\beta$ on holomorphic functions); $\hbar \neq 0$ is a fixed constant.
__notes__.note.correspondence.setting-statistics-r: The manner of the failure locates the true structure one level up: the palatial algebra cannot lie \emph{inside} the completion, so if the two are related at all, one must be built \emph{on} the other. The next two subsections prove that this is exactly what happens: the completion's fermionic quantisation produces twistor \emph{states}; the palatial bosonic quantisation then acts on those states.
__notes__.note.correspondence.point-contact-planes: Clause (1) is the classical statement that in six ambient dimensions every chiral spinor is pure (Cartan, Chevalley \cite{Chevalley54}); the annihilator planes of spinors in the conformal spinor space $\CS$ are one ruling family of maximal isotropic subspaces, in twistor language the $\alpha$-planes of complexified compactified Minkowski space, and the $\CSm$-family are the $\beta$-planes \cite{Penrose1967, PenroseRindler86}. The transport reading adds the physical origin: the three pairs of clause (2) are ladder pairs of exactly the kind the completion produces (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-ladder-pairs-fock-modules-over}), and the tower paper \cite[\S 4]{ButlerT3} shows each further ascent adjoins one more pair, doubling the half-spinor space: the tower is a qubit register, and the conformal spinor space (twistor space) is the chirality half of its three-qubit floor. \emph{First quantisation, in this precise sense, is the Chevalley functor from ambient directions to Fock states; it is forced at the singular locus by the no-go theorem} \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1}.
__notes__.note.lepton.abstract: The Standard-Model paper of the series proves that the tensor ledger of the minimal massive composite contains no lepton doublet, and declares a slot-statistics hypothesis (S) to supply one. This note asks whether the lepton can be derived inside the two-level hierarchy without it, and answers no, exactly. The ledger is the two-twistor Dirac space $\Sp \otimes \Sp$ with the automorphisms acting cell by cell; a lepton needs the slot to appear once with the pair state carrying the full system, $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ with the slot mixing acting once. That space is neither a subrepresentation of the ledger nor a consequence of the ladder theorem, proved for bare twistors, nor of the excitation theorem, which has no slot index. It is a hypothesis, here called (C), with one chirality bit left open, the slotted sector's handedness relative to the free sector; with the bit fixed by the anomalies, (C) is the one-constituent row of the slot-statistics hypothesis, weaker than it, departing from the ledger only on twistors with two or more pairs excited. Under (C) the content is $\C^{2} \otimes \T' = (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2}$, the quark and lepton doublets in one chirality half, $\C^{2} \otimes \T$ their duals. Two further results hold under (C) or (S) alike: in the untwisted action the constituent spectrum is self-conjugate exactly for the determinant-one group, which at the level of consistency with conjugation removes the thirteenth generator, which T12 now settles at proposition level; and the relative handedness of the two sectors is one bit, fixed by the anomalies. Every identity is verified by a deposited script.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-setting-what-importe: Everything here lives in the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12}, whose notation is used: the minimal massive hierarchy $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, two twistor slots of three ladder pairs each; the automorphism group $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ with its $U(1)$ factor written $(\lambda^{3}a, \lambda^{-2}b)$; the abelian weight $q$ and hypercharge $Y = q/6$; and the representation notation $(r_{2}, r_{3})_{Y}$. Six imports carry the argument.
__notes__.note.lepton.setting-constituent-space-hy:
The tensor ledger of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton} treats the six cells as independent fermionic modes: a state is an occupation pattern of cells, and a mixing of slots acts on each occupied cell separately. It is worth saying what this ledger is in the language of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}: $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \otimes W) = \Lambda^{\bullet}(W_{1} \oplus W_{2}) \cong \Sp_{1} \otimes \Sp_{2}$, the tensor product of the Dirac modules of the two twistors, each twistor excited by its own pair operators. Read on two twistors, Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} produces the ledger, not something else. A lepton doublet, $(2,1)$ of weight $-3$, needs a space in which the slot vector appears once and the pair state carries the full system; the ledger has no such space (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-tensor-ledger-contains-no-lepton}), and the natural candidate, $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ with the slot mixing acting on the slot alone, is not produced by the two theorems one would like to produce it. Fact \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} is proved for bare twistors, from their spinor parts, and says nothing about how a mixing acts on an excited twistor; Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} concerns one twistor and carries no slot index. The step between them is a premise, and the note states it as one.

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hypothesis (C), the constituent hypothesis.} A constituent of the composite is a Dirac state in a slot, a twistor or its partner with any of its pairs excited: its state space is
\[
\Con := \C^{2} \otimes \Sp = \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W,
\]
sixteen-dimensional, with a pair $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acting as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$: $A$ acts on the slot vector once, and on nothing else; $B$ acts on the Dirac state. The chirality of a constituent is that of the Dirac spinor it holds (Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations}) up to one overall sign $\epsilon = \pm 1$ for the slotted sector relative to the free sector: $\epsilon = +1$ means a slot leaves the half alone, $\epsilon = -1$ that it reverses it. (C) leaves $\epsilon$ open; Proposition \claimref{lepton.relative-handedness-slotted-free-sectors} fixes $\epsilon = -1$. Write $\Con_{k} := \C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$.
\end{quote}

Hypothesis (C) with $\epsilon = -1$ is the one-constituent row $j = 1$ of T12's Hypothesis (S), the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$: there the $(1, k)$ component is $\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ with exactly this action, and (S)'s chirality, the parity of $j + k$, is on that row the parity of $1 + k$, the reversed half, which is $\epsilon = -1$. With $\epsilon = +1$ the two would contradict each other on the chirality clause, which is why the bit is left open in (C) and fixed by an argument rather than stipulated. So fixed, (C) is weaker than (S) in the plain sense that (S) implies it: (C) says nothing about states with two slot modes, nothing about the statistics of pairs of constituents, and nothing about a composite state space at all. The note claims no minimality for (C) over any class of hypotheses; what it shows is that (C) is enough for the lepton (Proposition \claimref{lepton.content-constituent-space}) and exactly where any space holding one must depart from the ledger (Proposition \claimref{lepton.unit-action-cell-action}).

The automorphism group of Fact \claimref{lepton.imported-automorphism-group-section-hypercharge-generator} acts on $\Con$ through its canonical section: an automorphism is a $K$-coset of pairs, the coset's representative with $\det A \cdot \det B = 1$ is unique, and that representative acts as $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(B)$. the section “The group on the constituents, and the one remaining choice” shows that among the actions of the automorphism group on $\Con$ this is the only one compatible with conjugation.

The relation between $\Con$ and the tensor ledger is exact, and it is the precise sense in which the ledger has no lepton and (C) departs from it at one point only. It is also the independence witness for (C): the ledger is a structure satisfying Facts \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} and \claimref{lepton.imported-twistor-state-pair-system-excitations} in which the slot mixing acts cell by cell, so (C) is not a consequence of those Facts.

__notes__.note.mass.setting-exact-join: Theorem \claimref{mass.mass-weight-dictionary} and Proposition \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula} both compute a mass. This section shows that the flat-space formula is the squared pairing of the composite against the frozen point, extends it to $\Lambda \neq 0$ exactly, and then reads the composite's weight off the dictionary. The plan: find the frozen point of de Sitter space in the flat chart and fix what the chart's normalisation does and does not decide (Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}, Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes}); write the conformal generators in the chart (Lemma \claimref{mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism}); define the grip of a composite on the frozen point, which is its de Sitter momentum, and prove it is a real vector (Definition \claimref{obj.mass.grip-mass-composite}, Lemma \claimref{mass.grip-real}); compute its squared length in closed form (Theorem \claimref{mass.exact-join}); recognise the result as a difference of Casimirs (Proposition \claimref{mass.casimir-form-join}) and identify the five broken generators (Lemma \claimref{mass.five-broken-generators}); and read off the composite's weight (Proposition \claimref{mass.weight-composite}).
__notes__.note.mass.setting-conformal-generators-c: Write $\T = \Sc \oplus \Sc'$ with bases $e_{1}, e_{2}$ of $\Sc$ and $e_{3}, e_{4}$ of $\Sc'$, so that $n_{\infty} = e_{1}\wedge e_{2}$, $n_{0} = e_{3}\wedge e_{4}$, the $x$-slot is spanned by the mixed bivectors $e_{a}\wedge e_{a'}$ ($a \in \{1,2\}$, $a' \in \{3,4\}$), and $\varepsilon(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge e_{3}\wedge e_{4}) = 1$, which gives $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$. __notes__.note.odd-extensions.dictionary-ascents-n:
The correspondence between the frozen point and the pair the transport adjoins, stated in the root paper's normalisation (which fixes the null basis up to the dilation, one hyperbolic plane being isometric to any other). The adjoined plane has the signed basis $e_{\pm}$ and the null basis $v = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $v^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{+} - e_{-})$, with $v^{2} = v^{*2} = 0$ and $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, the pair the root paper adjoins and the tower paper reads as the one fermionic mode of the rung \cite[\S 2.2]{ButlerT1}, \cite[Prop.~4.1, Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3}. The note's canonical frame is the same two null rays, $v = I_{0}$ and $v^{*} = \varphi/2$. Then: at $\Lambda = 0$ the frozen point is the null generator $v$ itself, the zero divisor of vector type, and the direction the completion adjoins is its partner $v^{*}$, canonical by Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(i); the Stelle-West vector does not exist there. For $\Lambda \neq 0$ the frozen point is a combination of both null generators,
\[
I_{\Lambda} \;=\; \alpha\, v + \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \alpha\beta = \Lambda/3 ,
\]
and the Stelle-West vector is the same two components with the relative sign reversed,
\[
V \;\propto\; \alpha\, v - \beta\, v^{*}, \qquad Q(V) \propto -\alpha\beta ,
\]
orthogonal to $I_{\Lambda}$ and to the Lorentz frame. So $I$ and $V$ are the sum and difference of one pair of null components, which is why they form the signed basis up to scale and a boost (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}(i)); the sign of $\Lambda$ is the relative sign of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, de Sitter when they agree and anti-de Sitter when they differ, and the wall is either of them vanishing. The dilation acts as $v \mapsto tv$, $v^{*} \mapsto v^{*}/t$, an automorphism of the relation $vv^{*} + v^{*}v = 1$, and $\alpha\beta$ is its invariant (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gauge}); in the frame of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}, $\alpha = a$ and $\beta = 2b$. In the tower paper's reading of $v$ and $v^{*}$ as the annihilation and creation operators of the rung's mode, the frozen point of a $\Lambda = 0$ universe is a pure annihilator and a nonzero $\Lambda$ is a creation component, the product of the two coefficients being $\Lambda/3$; this is what that reading says verbatim; only the vanishing of the creation component is invariant, its size being the dilation gauge, and the note attaches no claim to the reading. The script verifies the null pair, its normalisation, the identification with the canonical frame, and the norms and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$ on instances of both signs and zero.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-two-negative: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii) says the frozen point's two components in the canonical null frame are related by a symmetry of the completion. __notes__.note.pairing.setting-two-claims-kill-con: The series' method is to state the conditions under which a claim dies before computing anything. __notes__.note.programme.setting-seventeen-refutat:
The series was produced by conjecturing naturally, failing precisely, and treating each failure as locating the next statement. Seventeen natural conjectures were attempted in the development of the programme; sixteen were refuted, and in every case the refutation located a better statement one level up, which is what a series paper now proves. The one exception is marked in the table: the twelfth conjecture, that $N$ is a parameter of the laws, is not refuted but placed, since the action paper proves it holds under the action as written, and whether $N$ is instead initial data of the descent rests on a promotion decision the series records open. The founding conjecture is the first and sets the pattern: it proposed that dividing by a zero divisor promotes the \emph{element}, that some enlarged algebra contains an inverse for the null vector. The truth is that nothing repairs the element, provably and permanently, and that the division instead promotes the \emph{space the element lies in}: the space completes, the value is taken at an adjoined ideal point, and the inverse operation never appears \cite{ButlerT1}. Everything else in the series is that first refutation iterated at larger scale.

Table \claimref{refuted.twistors-are-the-ladder-operators} is the refutation table: each refuted conjecture, the corrected statement that replaced it, and the series paper that now carries the correction as a result. The ordinals follow the order in which the conjectures were attempted during the programme's development; the fifth through seventeenth were numbered at the time, while rows 2 to 4 gather early corrections (among them the naive palatial identification, refuted by a statistics computation, and the natural form of the tautological twist, refuted by its own pairing argument) whose internal order is not insisted on. The discipline the table records has a methodological point worth stating plainly: a framework whose natural conjectures keep failing \emph{in a direction} is being determined by something. Sixteen consecutive failures, each of which made the surviving theory more falsifiable than the conjecture it replaced, are the series' best evidence that its subject is a structure and not a notation.

__notes__.note.rungs.compact-form: The ambient signature at rung two is $(4,6)$, whose spin group is the noncompact $\mathrm{Spin}(4,6)$; the group in Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3) is the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. __notes__.note.dark-tower-matter.why-u: (U1) and (U2) are how this tower does it: T12's constituent is one chirality half of the ascended spinor module, which is spin-irreducible \cite[Fact~2.2]{ButlerT12}; its $\C^{2}$ is two constituents and its $U(2)$ their momentum ladder; and T12 takes both factors' groups unitary. __notes__.note.standard-model.abstract: Mass first exists at two twistor constituents; this paper computes the composite's symmetries and finds the Standard Model. The minimal massive hierarchy is $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$; its automorphism algebra is $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ with global form $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, and only a two-by-three hierarchy has this algebra. Hypercharge is the weight of the abelian generator: the quark doublet at $Y = 1/6$ and the four singlets at $0, -2/3, 1/3, 1$, unconditionally; the lepton doublet needs one declared hypothesis, slot statistics, without which the state space holds no lepton. Under it the anomalies cancel, the generation is the half-spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ at unification; the one-loop run refutes the desert, so the running between scales must change. Partner content can do it: it must be split, the rows admissible at one loop decay the proton too fast, and the supersymmetric row is admissible at two loops. So can an intermediate symmetry: the automorphisms preserving the slot/pair split are Pati-Salam, broken with their left-right parity by the rung parity, and the chain meets six times above the proton bound, with the weak angle as an input that the fermion masses fit without tuning through a grade-three Georgi-Jarlskog direction. On the state space the Higgs doublet's representation is the directions transport adjoined; three no-go theorems show the Georgi-Jarlskog factor cannot come from the frozen point, the family structure or the bracket. The smallness problems are powers of $N = M_{P}/H$. Every identity is verified in exact arithmetic.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-prior-art: The prior work, acknowledged once. That the Standard Model's global gauge group is $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ with its $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ quotient and charge lattice, and that one generation with a right-handed neutrino is the even exterior algebra $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}\C^{5}$, the half-spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, is classical structure theory, expounded by Baez and Huerta \cite{BaezHuerta2010} and made more precise by Tong \cite{Tong2017}; the framework's claim is not the group, nor the exterior algebra, but their derivation from compositeness, and the paper says exactly which hypothesis that derivation needs. The unification value $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ and the one-loop running are the grand-unification literature's, from Georgi and Glashow \cite{GeorgiGlashow1974} through the precision-era analyses \cite{Amaldi1991}; anomaly-cancellation constraints on hypercharge are textbook \cite{WeinbergQFT2}. The two-twistor particle is the twistor literature's \cite{PenroseRindler1986}. What this paper claims as new is the derivation chain. The $U(n)$ ladder from momentum and helicity preservation. The minimal massive hierarchy $\C^{2}\otimes\C^{3}$, selected by the mass paper's theorem that mass begins at two constituents. The gauge algebra and exact global form as that hierarchy's automorphisms. The two-level fermion content, with the lepton doublet one level higher. Hypercharge as the weight of the global form's abelian generator, read off by pair counting, with the anomaly conditions as identities rather than inputs. The lepton doublet and the singlet listing under one declared hypothesis, slot statistics, and the proof that without it the state space contains no lepton. Chirality from the two halves of the single-twistor spinor module, and under (S) from the parity of the five-mode state space. The forced connection. And the compression of the numerical layer into the one number $N$ with its trichotomy.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-setting-impo: Notation follows the twistor and mass papers \cite{ButlerT9, ButlerT11}. The completion of the spacetime algebra is $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$, with ambient space $V = \R^{2,4}$ \cite[\S 2]{ButlerT9}; twistor space $\T$ is one chirality half of the ascended Dirac module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}); a twistor $Z = (\omega, \pi)$ carries the pair systems of the completion; $\bar{Z} \cdot Z$ is the Hermitian pairing. Four words are used throughout in fixed senses. A \emph{pair} is one fermionic ladder pair (one creation and one annihilation operator) of the completion. A \emph{level} of the hierarchy is a tier of the partition of a composite into twistors and of each twistor into its pairs; the twistor paper's word for the same tiers is \emph{storey}, kept where that paper is quoted. This fixed sense is the tower level; the paper's epistemic phrases, ``record level'', ``observation level'', ``assembly level'' and the levels of the results in the section “The levels of the results, and successor problems”, use the word in the series' other sense, the standard at which a statement is established. The \emph{state space} of a system is the Fock space its pairs generate, in the sense of the tower paper \cite{ButlerT3}; from the section “The one number” the paper also refers to the boundary mode space of the cosmological horizon, in the sense of the entropy paper \cite{ButlerT8}, and the text says which space is meant. __notes__.note.standard-model.sixth-refutation-lad: The natural conjecture, that the ladder of Proposition \claimref{standard-model.internal-symmetry-ladder} is the Standard Model gauge group, fails structurally, and for the sixth time in the series (the capstone keeps the count \cite{ButlerT17}) the failure makes the question more precise. The ladder's three groups act on \emph{different sectors}, indexed by constituent number, whereas $SU(3) \times SU(2) \times U(1)$ acts on all matter simultaneously as a direct product. What survives the refutation is the architecture: a fundamental matter unit built of up to three conformal spinors, each itself the vacuum of three pairs (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), carries a two-level hierarchy of pairs, and the corrected conjecture is that the physical gauge group is the automorphism group of that hierarchy: the mixings respecting both levels of the partition. the section “The gauge algebra and the global form” proves the corrected conjecture's algebra and determines its global form; the representation content is the section “Content, charges, chirality”'s. Everything in this remark past the two propositions is at observation level, and is flagged as such.

__notes__.note.field-theory.what-does-t12: T12's orientation bit, which the dark-matter paper shows the descent cannot derive, is not removed by $i = I_4$; it moves into the relative sign of the conformal spinors' unit ($\pm I_6$, the twistor's unit) and the field's. If the series fixes that sign, and if the label copy's parity is identified with the conformal spinors' (the twistor's; the theorem T12 calls the same missing theorem as Hypothesis (S)), the orientation is fixed, through T12's Fact on the charge and helicity read on the conformal spinor space (twistor charge and helicity), whose conventions were not checked here. Its physical content would be at most the sign of CP violation.
__notes__.note.standard-model.setting-content-char: At observation level, and flagged as such: the weak coupling is chiral because the automorphisms act on states of definite chirality, and under (S) every state of the composite has one, the parity of its mode number; which parity is called left-handed is the identification of the one-handed listing of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency} with the Standard Model's left-handed convention, and it is the same choice as the orientation. That twistor charge is helicity (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-twistor-charge-helicity}) is what ties the parity of the single-twistor sector to spacetime handedness; the extension of that tie to the five-mode parity of (S) is part of what (S) asserts.
__notes__.note.synthesis.n-plus-orientation-datum: Premise (N$_{+}$) (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}) assumes the orientation of the field's unit $I_{4}$ relative to the time orientation, which decides between the null vacuum and the filled positive-energy sea. Three facts now locate that datum. First, with the unit $I_{4}$ every massless mode's helicity is locked to its frequency sign, every map commuting with the Lorentz rotors is $I_{4}$-linear, and among the discrete maps of the massless field the frequency sign flips exactly under reversal of spatial orientation; Hestenes' charge conjugation flips the chirality of massless even spinors and not the frequency sign, and a CP map flips the frequency sign and not the chirality (\claimref{synthesis.massless-frequency-sign-relative-to-i4-is-not-the-chirality}). So the datum is odd under P and under CP, it is not that chirality, and no CP-invariant interaction fixes it. Second, on the Witt flags of $\R^{2,4}$ adapted to the conformal energy, the energy sign of a flag's vacuum and the stored flag bit flip together on each pair of conjugate flags (\claimref{synthesis.z-adapted-witt-flags-energy-sign-follows-the-flag-bit}), so read as the energy sign of the flag's vacuum the datum is the descent's flag bit (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}) up to the descent's kinematic sign on the four-space orthogonal to $Z$. Third, on every field the Hadamard deposit premise reaches, the datum is carried by that premise, through results that rest on no postulate (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}). What is not shown is that the generators' modes inherit the descent's flag; on the eternal hole and eternal de Sitter, which no descent reaches, the datum stays assumed.

correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spa.technical:
Let $\mathfrak{l} = \Lambda^2(W_{1,3})_\C$ be the complexified Lorentz algebra of the splitting, written as the sum $\mathfrak{g}^+\oplus\mathfrak{g}^-$ of two commuting copies of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ supplied by the chirality split, acting on $W_\C = (W_{1,3})_\C$ and on the planes $\Som$, $\Spi$ of the conformal spinor space. Then $\omega\otimes\pi \mapsto \Psi^{-1}(\omega\wedge\pi)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathfrak{l}$-modules $\Som\otimes\Spi \cong W_\C$, and one of $\mathfrak{g}^\pm$ acts faithfully on $\Som$ and trivially on $\Spi$ while the other does the reverse: the two planes are the two chiral doublets.

Moreover the spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{l}}(W_\C\otimes\Spi, \Som)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak{l}}(W_\C\otimes\Som, \Spi)$ are each one-dimensional, so a Lorentz-equivariant map of either type is unique up to a scalar.
correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spa.lay: The Lorentz symmetry of spacetime, once complex numbers are allowed, splits into two independent halves. This result shows that the two planes into which the spinor space of the conformal algebra splits are exactly the basic two-component objects of these halves, one plane for each, and that together they rebuild the spacetime directions. It also shows that there is essentially only one symmetric way to combine a spacetime direction with one plane so as to land in the other.
correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spa.typing_note: Added the chirality split because the statement takes its commuting decomposition as a hypothesis and the proof's ideal argument rests on it; the skew-lines edge is a real premise (mixed slot equals the image of W_C).

proofs.main:
Two preliminaries. First, $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ is simple: with the standard basis $e, h, f$, an ideal containing $x = ae + bh + cf \neq 0$ contains $[e,[e,x]] = -2c\,e$ and $[f,[f,x]] = -2a\,f$, so it contains $e$ or $f$ unless $a = c = 0$, in which case it contains $h$ and then $[h,e] = 2e$; and from any one of $e, f, h$ the brackets $[e,f] = h$, $[h,e] = 2e$, $[h,f] = -2f$ produce the other two. Second, the ideals of $\mathfrak{l} = \mathfrak{g}^+\oplus\mathfrak{g}^-$ are $0$, $\mathfrak{g}^+$, $\mathfrak{g}^-$, $\mathfrak{l}$: if an ideal $I$ is not contained in $\mathfrak{g}^-$, its projection to $\mathfrak{g}^+$ is a nonzero ideal of $\mathfrak{g}^+$, hence all of $\mathfrak{g}^+$, and then $\mathfrak{g}^+ = [\mathfrak{g}^+, \mathfrak{g}^+] = [\mathfrak{g}^+, I] \subseteq I$ (the $\mathfrak{g}^-$-components of $I$ commute with $\mathfrak{g}^+$, by \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}(1)); symmetrically for $\mathfrak{g}^-$.

(1) The Levi factor stabilises the rays of $\nO$ and $\nInf$, so by equivariance of $\Psi$ it preserves the planes $\Spi$ and $\Som$, and $\mathfrak{l}$ acts on both. The map $\omega\otimes\pi \mapsto \omega\wedge\pi$ is equivariant for the induced action on $\Lambda^2\CS$ (the action for which $\Psi$ is equivariant) and surjective onto the four-dimensional mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi = \Psi(W_\C)$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}), so by dimension $\Som\otimes\Spi \cong W_\C$ as $\mathfrak{l}$-modules. The action of $\mathfrak{l}$ on $W_\C$ is faithful (bivectors act on vectors as $\so(V)$, \claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}, read over $\C$): the bivector $e_i\wedge e_j$ of an orthonormal pair acts as $\pm$ the elementary antisymmetric matrix, and the six are linearly independent. Let $\mathfrak{k}_\omega, \mathfrak{k}_\pi \subseteq \mathfrak{l}$ be the kernels of the actions on $\Som$, $\Spi$: ideals. Each is nonzero, since $\dim\mathfrak{l} = 6 > 4 = \dim\mathfrak{gl}(2,\C)$. Neither is $\mathfrak{l}$: if $\mathfrak{l}$ annihilated $\Spi$ it would act on $W_\C \cong \Som\otimes\Spi$ through $\Som$ alone, with image of dimension at most $4 < 6$, contradicting faithfulness; likewise for $\Som$. So $\mathfrak{k}_\omega, \mathfrak{k}_\pi \in \{\mathfrak{g}^+, \mathfrak{g}^-\}$, and they are different, since a common kernel would annihilate $\Som\otimes\Spi = W_\C$. Say $\mathfrak{k}_\pi = \mathfrak{g}^a$ and $\mathfrak{k}_\omega = \mathfrak{g}^b$ with $\{a, b\} = \{+,-\}$. The kernel of $\mathfrak{g}^b$ acting on $\Spi$ is an ideal of $\mathfrak{g}^b$, hence $0$ or $\mathfrak{g}^b$, and not $\mathfrak{g}^b$ (then $\mathfrak{l} = \mathfrak{g}^a + \mathfrak{g}^b$ would annihilate $\Spi$); so $\mathfrak{g}^b$ acts faithfully on $\Spi$, and likewise $\mathfrak{g}^a$ on $\Som$. The verification script exhibits the assignment in the Fock model.

(2) Keep the labelling of (1). A faithful action of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ on a $2$-plane $S$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathfrak{sl}(S)$: the image is three-dimensional and consists of traceless operators, because $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C) = [\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C), \mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)]$ and commutators are traceless, and $\dim\mathfrak{sl}(S) = 3$. An $\mathfrak{l}$-equivariant map $f: W_\C\otimes\Spi \cong \Som\otimes\Spi\otimes\Spi \to \Som$ is therefore a linear map that commutes with $\mathfrak{sl}(\Som)$ acting on the first factor (through $\mathfrak{g}^a$, which acts trivially on the $\Spi$ factors) and is annihilated by $\mathfrak{sl}(\Spi)$ acting as a derivation on the last two factors (through $\mathfrak{g}^b$, trivial on $\Som$). Regard $f$ as a bilinear map $\Spi\times\Spi \to \End(\Som)$, $(\pi,\pi') \mapsto (\omega \mapsto f(\omega\otimes\pi\otimes\pi'))$. Its values commute with $\mathfrak{sl}(\Som)$, hence are scalars (an operator commuting with $E_{12}$, $E_{21}$ and $E_{11} - E_{22}$ is scalar), so $f$ is a bilinear form $\beta$ on $\Spi$ with $\beta(X\pi, \pi') + \beta(\pi, X\pi') = 0$ for all $X \in \mathfrak{sl}(\Spi)$. In a basis $\pi_1, \pi_2$ with $h = \operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ and $e = E_{12}$: $h$-invariance gives $2\beta(\pi_1,\pi_1) = 0 = -2\beta(\pi_2,\pi_2)$, and $e$-invariance applied to $(\pi_2, \pi_2)$ gives $\beta(\pi_1,\pi_2) + \beta(\pi_2,\pi_1) = 0$. So $\beta$ is a multiple of the determinant form, which is invariant; the space is one-dimensional. The other case is the same with the roles of the planes exchanged.

correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-.technical:
The complexified Lorentz subalgebra $\mathfrak{l} = \Lambda^2(W_{1,3})_\C \cong \mathfrak{so}(1,3)_\C$ splits into the $\pm i$ eigenspaces $\mathfrak{g}^\pm$ of the duality operator. Each is a subalgebra isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$, and $[\mathfrak{g}^+, \mathfrak{g}^-] = 0$: the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors commute.

In the palatial algebra $\mathcal{P}$ let $\mathcal{A}^-$ be the unital subalgebra generated by $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^-))$, and call $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^+))$ the googly slot. Every ordering discrepancy of a word in $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^-))$ lies in $\hbar\,\mathcal{A}^-$, and for two letters it is exactly $\hbar\,q(\rho([P,Q]))$; $\mathcal{A}^-$ commutes with the googly slot; and under the adjoint action of $\mathfrak{g}^+$ through $q\circ\rho/\hbar$, $\mathcal{P}$ is locally finite, the googly slot is a copy of the adjoint representation, and every element of $\mathcal{A}^-$ has zero component in the adjoint isotypic subspace. So reorderings within the anti-self-dual sector never source the googly slot, at quartic or any other order.
correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-.lay: The symmetries of spacetime, extended to complex numbers, fall into two halves that do not interact, called self-dual and anti-self-dual. In Penrose's palatial algebra, a noncommutative algebra of operators built on the conformal spinor coordinates, changing the order of operators built from one half only ever produces more operators from that same half. Such reorderings therefore never feed into the slot where the other half's information, the so-called googly data, would sit, however many operators are involved.

proofs.main:
(1) Fix the orientation of $W_{1,3}$ given by the ordered basis $a_2, b_2, b_3, b_4$ of the section “Setting and imports”, written $e_0, \dots, e_3$ below. With boosts $B_i := e_0\wedge e_i$ and rotations $R_i := e_j\wedge e_k$ ($(i,j,k)$ cyclic), the $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ brackets, the commutators of bivectors (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}), are $[R_i, R_j] = \epsilon_{ijk}R_k$, $[R_i, B_j] = \epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, $[B_i, B_j] = -\epsilon_{ijk}R_k$ (the first two are rotations acting on vectors and axial pairs; the third is the boost-boost computation of \cite[Lem.~5.4]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.boosts-generate-exactly-levi-factor}), reproved by the script). Setting $A^{(1)}_i := \tfrac12(R_i + iB_i)$, $A^{(2)}_i := \tfrac12(R_i - iB_i)$ and using $[B_i, R_j] = +\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$,
\begin{gather*}
[A^{(1)}_i, A^{(1)}_j] = \tfrac14\,\epsilon_{ijk}\bigl(R_k + iB_k + iB_k + R_k\bigr) = \epsilon_{ijk}A^{(1)}_k,\\
[A^{(1)}_i, A^{(2)}_j] = \tfrac14\,\epsilon_{ijk}\bigl(R_k - iB_k + iB_k - R_k\bigr) = 0,
\end{gather*}
and likewise $[A^{(2)}_i, A^{(2)}_j] = \epsilon_{ijk}A^{(2)}_k$; the script verifies all fifteen brackets of the $R, B$ table and the nine cross brackets exactly. Duality: $\ast B_i = -R_i$, $\ast R_i = B_i$ (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.lorentzian-duality-complex-structure}), so $\ast A^{(1)}_i = \tfrac12(B_i - iR_i) = -iA^{(1)}_i$ and $\ast A^{(2)}_i = +iA^{(2)}_i$: $\mathfrak{g}^+$ is spanned by the $A^{(2)}_i$ and $\mathfrak{g}^-$ by the $A^{(1)}_i$. Which eigenspace is called self-dual is a convention, and nothing below depends on it.
(2) (a) Two orderings of a word $q(\rho(P_1))\cdots q(\rho(P_r))$, $P_s \in \mathfrak{g}^-$, differ by a sequence of adjacent transpositions, each of which changes the word by the word with the adjacent pair $q(\rho(P_s))q(\rho(P_t))$ replaced by $[q(\rho(P_s)), q(\rho(P_t))] = \hbar\,q(\rho([P_s, P_t]))$ (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(2) and Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}); since $[P_s, P_t] \in \mathfrak{g}^-$ by (1), the result is $\hbar$ times a word in elements of $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^-))$, an element of $\hbar\,\mathcal{A}^-$; for $r = 2$ it is the single commutator displayed. (b) For $P \in \mathfrak{g}^-$ and $Q \in \mathfrak{g}^+$, $[q(\rho(P)), q(\rho(Q))] = \hbar\,q(\rho([P,Q])) = 0$ by (1); the centraliser of $q(\rho(\mathfrak{g}^+))$ is a unital subalgebra containing the generators of $\mathcal{A}^-$, hence $\mathcal{A}^-$. (c) By Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(1), $\operatorname{ad}_{q(\rho(Q))}/\hbar$ acts on the generators $Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta$ linearly, so it preserves the span $F_k$ of the words of length at most $k$; each $F_k$ is finite-dimensional, so $\mathcal{P} = \bigcup_k F_k$ is a locally finite $\mathfrak{g}^+$-module and Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-complete-reducibility} decomposes each $F_k$, compatibly, into isotypic components; write $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}^{\mathfrak{g}^+} \oplus \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{ad}} \oplus \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rest}}$ for the trivial, adjoint and remaining isotypic parts. The map $Q \mapsto q(\rho(Q))$ intertwines the adjoint representation of $\mathfrak{g}^+$ with the adjoint action on $\mathcal{P}$ (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(2)) and is injective, so the googly slot is an irreducible subrepresentation isomorphic to the adjoint one, hence contained in $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{ad}}$. By (b), $\mathcal{A}^- \subseteq \mathcal{P}^{\mathfrak{g}^+}$, and $\mathcal{P}^{\mathfrak{g}^+} \cap (\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{ad}} \oplus \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{rest}}) = 0$; so every element of $\mathcal{A}^-$ has zero adjoint-isotypic component, whatever its degree.

correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-sh.formal:
Let $(v, v^*)$ be a null pair of $V$ with $\ip{v}{v^*} = 1$ (an adjoined ladder pair), and let $E := v\wedge v^* \in \mathfrak{so}(2,4)$ be the grading element of the corresponding hyperbolic plane. In the Fock model, the spinor action of $E$ is
\[
\rho(E) \;=\; \tfrac12\,c(v)\,c(v^*) - \tfrac12 \;=\; N - \tfrac12 ,
\]
where $N$ is the occupation number operator of the mode created by $v$ (eigenvalue $1$ on states containing that mode, $0$ otherwise). The generator of the adjoined plane's boost is the mode's number operator shifted by one half.
correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-sh.technical:
Take a null pair $(v, v^*)$ of $V$ with $\ip{v}{v^*} = 1$, an adjoined ladder pair, and let $E = v\wedge v^*$ be the grading element of its hyperbolic plane in $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$. In the Fock model its spinor action is $\rho(E) = \tfrac12 c(v)c(v^*) - \tfrac12 = N - \tfrac12$, where $N$ is the occupation number of the mode created by $v$, equal to $1$ on states containing that mode and $0$ otherwise.

So the boost generator of the adjoined plane is the mode's number operator shifted by one half.
correspondence.clifford-side-ordering-sh.lay: Each extra pair of directions added by the completion behaves like a single fermionic mode, which can be empty or occupied. The symmetry that stretches this pair of directions acts on spinors as the number of particles in that mode minus one half. The leftover half is a fixed offset, one half per mode.

proofs.main: The bivector element of $\Cl(V_\C)$ attached to $a\wedge b$ is $\tfrac12 c(a)c(b) - \tfrac12\ip{a}{b}$ (the product of two vectors is $\ip{a}{b}$ plus half their commutator, \claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}): its commutator with vectors is the bivector action for any $a, b$, orthogonal or not, as in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}. Take $v = w_1$, $v^* = w_1'$ in an adapted model, and write $A_1 := w_1\wedge(\cdot)$, $B_1 := \iota_{w_1'}$, so $c(v)c(v^*) = 2\,A_1 B_1$. On a basis monomial containing $w_1$, $A_1B_1$ removes and restores the $w_1$-factor: eigenvalue $1$; on a monomial without $w_1$, $B_1$ annihilates it: eigenvalue $0$. So $\tfrac12 c(v)c(v^*) = N$ and $\rho(E) = N - \tfrac12$. The script checks the full $8\times 8$ eigenvalue table. The eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac12$ on the two chirality-plane pairs are the grading weights used in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.local-twistor-transport-ascended-spinor-connection}.

correspondence.fock-model-complexified-a.formal:
Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in W \oplus W' = V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an algebra map $\Cl(V_\C) \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$; this map is an isomorphism, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion. Vectors act oddly, so the even and odd halves
\[
\CS := \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} W, \qquad \CSm := \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}} W,
\]
each of complex dimension 4, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS) \oplus \End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space $\CS$ and its opposite $\CSm$ (twistor and dual twistor space).
correspondence.fock-model-complexified-a.technical:
Choose a maximal totally isotropic subspace $W \subset V_\C$, of complex dimension three, and a dual isotropic complement $W'$; such pairs exist and any two are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$. On $\Lambda^\bullet W$, of dimension $8$, set $c(w) = \sqrt2\,w\wedge(\cdot)$ for $w \in W$ and $c(w') = \sqrt2\,\iota_{w'}$ for $w' \in W'$. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an isomorphism $\Cl(V_\C) \cong \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion.

Vectors act oddly, so the even and odd parts $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, each of dimension four, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS)\oplus\End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space and its opposite.
correspondence.fock-model-complexified-a.lay: The completed algebra of six directions can be represented concretely. Pick three complex directions that are mutually lightlike, and let the algebra act on all combinations of them by adding or removing a direction, much as one creates and destroys particles. This gives an eight-dimensional space on which the algebra acts faithfully and irreducibly, the only such space up to equivalence, and it splits into two four-dimensional halves, the two chiralities.
