mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism.technical:
Write $\CS = \Som \oplus \Spi$ with $n_\infty = e_1 \wedge e_2$, $n_0 = e_3 \wedge e_4$, and the $x$-slot spanned by the mixed bivectors $e_a \wedge e_{a'}$. Under the isomorphism $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS) \to \so(\Lambda^2\CS, \varepsilon)$, the bivector $n_\infty \wedge n_0$ corresponds to the grading element $\operatorname{diag}(-\tfrac12, -\tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac12)$.

The translations $x \wedge n_\infty$ correspond to the upper off-diagonal block $b_x : \Spi \to \Som$, $(b_x\pi)^a = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\pi^{b'}$, and the special conformal generators $x \wedge n_0$ to the lower block $c_x : \Som \to \Spi$, $(c_x\omega)^{a'} = -x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\omega^a$. The proof checks on each basis bivector that the displayed matrix acts as the named rotation.
mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism.lay: The conformal symmetries of spacetime can be written either as rotations of a six-dimensional space or as four-by-four matrices acting on the four-component spinors of the conformal algebra. This lemma writes that translation out explicitly in the chart used for spacetime points. Dilations become a diagonal matrix, translations an upper corner block, and special conformal transformations a lower corner block.
mass.chart-form-spin-isomorphism.typing_note: The proof starts from the spin isomorphism and the chart normalisation recorded in the flat-model fact, so that fact was added as the premise; the remark on nullity it also cites is not in the store.

proofs.main:
Since the map $A \mapsto (U \mapsto A\cdot U)$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathfrak{so}(\Lambda^{2}\CS,\varepsilon)$ (Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}), it suffices to check that each displayed matrix acts on the six basis bivectors as the named rotation does. Throughout, $Q(n_{\infty}) = Q(n_{0}) = 0$, $\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = 1$, and the $x$-slot is orthogonal to both.

(1) $R_{n_{\infty}\wedge n_{0}}$ sends $n_{\infty} \mapsto Q(n_{\infty})n_{0} - \ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}}n_{\infty} = -n_{\infty}$, $n_{0} \mapsto n_{0}$, and every $x$-slot vector to $0$. The matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$ sends $e_{1}\wedge e_{2} \mapsto (-\tfrac12 - \tfrac12)e_{1}\wedge e_{2} = -n_{\infty}$, $e_{3}\wedge e_{4} \mapsto n_{0}$, and $e_{a}\wedge e_{a'} \mapsto (-\tfrac12 + \tfrac12)e_{a}\wedge e_{a'} = 0$.

(2) $R_{x\wedge n_{\infty}}$ sends $n_{\infty} \mapsto \ip{x}{n_{\infty}}n_{\infty} - Q(n_{\infty})x = 0$, a mixed bivector $y \mapsto \ip{x}{y}n_{\infty}$, and $n_{0} \mapsto \ip{x}{n_{0}}n_{\infty} - \ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}}x = -x$. The matrix $A$ with block $b_{x}$ annihilates $\Som$ and maps $e_{b'} \mapsto x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{a'b'}e_{a}$. Hence $A\cdot n_{\infty} = Ae_{1}\wedge e_{2} + e_{1}\wedge Ae_{2} = 0$. For $y = e_{c}\wedge e_{b'}$: $A\cdot y = e_{c}\wedge Ae_{b'} = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\,e_{c}\wedge e_{a} = x^{aa'}\varepsilon_{a'b'}\varepsilon_{ca}\,n_{\infty}$, while by Remark \claimref{note.mass.what-nullity-fixes} $\ip{x}{e_{c}\wedge e_{b'}} = -\varepsilon_{ac}\varepsilon_{a'b'}x^{aa'} = \varepsilon_{ca}\varepsilon_{a'b'}x^{aa'}$: equal. For $n_{0}$: $A\cdot(e_{3}\wedge e_{4}) = Ae_{3}\wedge e_{4} + e_{3}\wedge Ae_{4} = x^{a4}\varepsilon_{43}\,e_{a}\wedge e_{4} + x^{a3}\varepsilon_{34}\,e_{3}\wedge e_{a} = -x^{a4}e_{a}\wedge e_{4} - x^{a3}e_{a}\wedge e_{3} = -x$.

(3) $R_{x\wedge n_{0}}$ sends $n_{0} \mapsto 0$, $y \mapsto \ip{x}{y}n_{0}$, and $n_{\infty} \mapsto \ip{x}{n_{\infty}}n_{0} - \ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}}x = -x$. The matrix with block $c_{x}$ annihilates $\Spi$ and maps $e_{a} \mapsto -x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}e_{a'}$. Hence $A\cdot n_{0} = 0$. For $y = e_{a}\wedge e_{c'}$: $A\cdot y = Ae_{a}\wedge e_{c'} = -x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\,e_{a'}\wedge e_{c'} = -x^{ba'}\varepsilon_{ba}\varepsilon_{a'c'}\,n_{0}$, while $\ip{x}{e_{a}\wedge e_{c'}} = -\varepsilon_{ba}\varepsilon_{a'c'}x^{ba'}$: equal. For $n_{\infty}$: $A\cdot(e_{1}\wedge e_{2}) = Ae_{1}\wedge e_{2} + e_{1}\wedge Ae_{2} = -x^{2a'}\varepsilon_{21}\,e_{a'}\wedge e_{2} - x^{1a'}\varepsilon_{12}\,e_{1}\wedge e_{a'} = -x^{2a'}e_{2}\wedge e_{a'} - x^{1a'}e_{1}\wedge e_{a'} = -x$.

Each displayed matrix is traceless. The script solves the linear systems $A\cdot P = R(P)$ exactly for the nine rotations displayed and confirms that the solutions are these matrices, entry by entry.

mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-i.formal: On a region where the gravitational field is a pure dilation $\hb = \sigma$ of the flat background in some gauge (so the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes; derived metric $\sigma^{-2}\eta$) the ambient bundle is trivial: its fibre is one fixed vector space $V$ with the ambient pairing, parallel sections are constant vectors, and the canonical tractor at the point $x$ is $X(x) = n_{0} + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)\, n_{\infty}$, with $n_{0}, n_{\infty}$ null, $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = +1$, $x$ in their orthogonal complement, and $Q(x) = \ip{x}{x} = g(x,x)$ the flat quadratic form, so that $Q(X(x)) = 0$ identically. The scale function of a constant vector $V$ is its $\sigma$-slot in the flat scale, $\sigma_{V}(x) = \ip{X(x)}{V}$. The complexification of $V$ is $\Lambda^{2}\CS$ for $\CS$ the conformal spinor space (twistor space; the chirality half of the ascended Dirac module), with pairing $\ip{U}{U'} = \varepsilon(U \wedge U')$ for the volume form $\varepsilon$ on $\Lambda^{4}\CS$ that the identification fixes; a bivector is simple iff its norm vanishes; the mixed slot carries $Q(x) = -2\det x$ in the chart's components \cite[Thm.~4.2(2)]{ButlerT9}; a conformal spinor splits as $Z = (\omega, \pi)$ with $\omega$ in the two-plane $\Som$ whose Pl\"ucker bivector is $n_{\infty}$ and $\pi$ in the two-plane $\Spi$ whose Pl\"ucker bivector is $n_{0}$. The action of $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ on $\Lambda^{2}\CS$ by $A\cdot(u \wedge v) = Au \wedge v + u \wedge Av$ is a Lie algebra isomorphism onto $\mathfrak{so}(\Lambda^{2}\CS, \varepsilon)$, and the infinity bivector of a scale (the infinity twistor) is the image of its scale tractor: for a vacuum with $\Lambda = 0$ it is covariantly constant and simple, the Pl\"ucker bivector of the infinity line. \emph{Provenance:} the flat model as a fixed vector space with the point embedding is \cite[\S4.2]{ButlerT6}, the scale function $\sigma = \ip{X}{I}$ recovering $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is used in \cite[Lem.~4.8]{ButlerT6}, and the general form of the dictionary (parallel sections are constant vectors, with $\sigma$-slot $\ip{X(x)}{V}$) is \cite[\S2]{BEG1994}; in the form needed here it is elementary and is proved in one paragraph inside Lemma \claimref{mass.de-sitter-scale-frozen-point}; the chirality half is \cite[Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT9}; the identification $V_{\C} = \Lambda^{2}\CS$ with its pairing, the normalisation of $\varepsilon$, the simplicity criterion, and the equivariance of the identification are \cite[Thm.~3.4]{ButlerT9}; the chart, the identification of the incidence relation with the completion's own chart, the spin isomorphism, and the infinity bivector are \cite[Thm.~4.2, Cor.~4.8, Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT9}, in that paper's sign conventions, machine-verified there. The spinor bracket $\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} = \varepsilon^{AB}\pi^{1}_{A}\pi^{2}_{B}$, the null momentum $p_{AA'} = \pi_{A}\bar\pi_{A'}$ of a conformal spinor, and the conformal generators as Hermitian quadratics $\bar{Z}_{\alpha}Z^{\beta}$ in the conformal spinor variables are classical \cite{PenroseRindler1986, Hughston1979}.
mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-i.technical:
On a region where the gravitational field is a pure dilation $\hb = \sigma$ of the flat background in some gauge (so the Weyl part of the field strength vanishes; derived metric $\sigma^{-2}\eta$) the ambient bundle is trivial with one fixed fibre $V$: parallel sections are constant vectors, the canonical tractor is $X(x) = n_0 + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)\,n_\infty$ with $n_0, n_\infty$ null and $\ip{n_0}{n_\infty} = 1$, so $Q(X(x)) = 0$, and a constant vector $V$ has scale function $\sigma_V(x) = \ip{X(x)}{V}$.

Complexified, $V_\C = \Lambda^2\CS$ with $\ip{U}{U'} = \varepsilon(U \wedge U')$; null bivectors are exactly the simple ones, the mixed slot carries $Q(x) = -2\det x$, and a conformal spinor splits as $Z = (\omega, \pi)$ along the planes of $n_\infty$ and $n_0$. The action of $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ on $\Lambda^2\CS$ is an isomorphism onto $\so(\Lambda^2\CS, \varepsilon)$, and the infinity bivector of a scale is its scale tractor, covariantly constant and simple when $\Lambda = 0$. Classical ingredients from twistor theory (the spinor bracket, the null momentum $p_{AA'} = \pi_A\bar\pi_{A'}$, the generators as Hermitian quadratics) are imported alongside.
mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-i.lay: This gathers in one place the flat-space set-up that the mass paper builds on. A point of flat spacetime is represented by a light-like vector in a six-dimensional space, and that space can be rebuilt from pairs of four-component spinors of the conformal algebra. In this picture the conformal symmetries act on those spinors as matrices, and the bivector at infinity that records the choice of scale is, when the cosmological constant vanishes, a fixed line in the projective spinor space.

mass.imported-palatial-quadratics-homoge.formal: The symmetrised quadratics $q(M)$ in the palatial oscillators $Z^\alpha$, $\bar Z_\beta$ (twistor oscillators: the conformal spinor coordinates and their conjugates) represent $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ with $[q(M), q(M')] = \hbar\, q([M,M'])$, and, in that paper's realisation $\bar{Z}_{\beta} = -\hbar\partial_{\beta}$, the symmetrised identity quadratic $q(\mathrm{id})$ acts on functions of homogeneity $h$ as $-(h+2)\hbar$ (Penrose's $-2s-2$, proved in the series as an exact identity in the proof of that theorem); the lemma represents all of $\mathfrak{gl}(4,\C)$, of which $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ is the real form used here. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lem.~5.5, Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9}. Used here only in Remark \claimref{note.mass.quantisation-ordering}, to place the classical computation of the section “The exact join” against its quantisation.
mass.imported-palatial-quadratics-homoge.technical:
The symmetrised quadratics $q(M)$ in the palatial oscillators represent $\mathfrak{gl}(4, \C)$, and hence its real form $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, with $[q(M), q(M')] = \hbar\, q([M, M'])$.

In the realisation $\bar Z_\beta = -\hbar\partial_\beta$, the symmetrised identity quadratic acts on functions homogeneous of degree $h$ as $q(\mathrm{id}) = -(h+2)\hbar$, which is Penrose's homogeneity $-2s-2$. Here it is used only to set a classical computation against its quantisation.
mass.imported-palatial-quadratics-homoge.lay: When the coordinates of the four-component conformal spinors are turned into quantum operators, certain quadratic combinations of them reproduce the conformal symmetry algebra. One of them, built from the identity, measures how a function on the spinor space scales, shifted by two because of operator ordering. This matches Penrose's rule relating scaling weight to helicity.

odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gaug.technical:
In the hyperbolic plane orthogonal to the Lorentz frame take $I = (e_+ + e_-)/2$ and $\varphi = e_+ - e_-$. The bivector $B = I \wedge \varphi = -e_+e_-$ satisfies $B^2 = +1$, commutes with every Lorentz vector and bivector, and anticommutes with $e_\pm$, so it generates the dilations of the conformal model. The rotor $R = \cosh\theta + B\sinh\theta$ fixes the Lorentz frame and acts by $I \mapsto tI$, $\varphi \mapsto \varphi/t$ with $t = e^{2\theta}$, so the boosts that move the frozen point are dilations.

Hence the ratio $b/a$ of the frozen point's components is a dilation gauge and only $2ab = \Lambda/3$ is invariant. Since the point at infinity has no physical fluctuation, the dynamics does not fix this gauge either, and the frame that the transport supplies carries no quantity beyond $\Lambda$.
odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gaug.lay: The frozen point is described by two numbers, but a change of overall scale (a dilation) can trade one for the other while keeping their product fixed. This result shows that the freedom the transport leaves is exactly such a change of scale. So only the product, which is set by the cosmological constant, has physical meaning.
odd-extensions.boost-dilation-ratio-gaug.typing_note: Both uses are cited in the proof of clause (iii) and kept; no context references or repairs to review. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: (i) $I\varphi = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})(e_{+} - e_{-}) = 1 - e_{+}e_{-}$, so $I \wedge \varphi = -e_{+}e_{-}$ and $B^{2} = -e_{+}^{2}e_{-}^{2} = +1$; a bivector of a plane commutes with vectors orthogonal to the plane and anticommutes with vectors in it (\claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute}). (ii) $R = \cosh\theta + B\sinh\theta$ is the exponential of the bivector $\theta B$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-exponential}), and $R\tilde R = \cosh^{2}\theta - \sinh^{2}\theta = 1$, $R$ fixes what commutes with $B$, and on the plane $RxR^{-1}$ is the hyperbolic rotation by $2\theta$, whose eigenvectors are the null directions with eigenvalues $e^{\pm 2\theta}$. (iii) is (ii) with Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii) and Fact \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation}. The script verifies (i) and (ii) with the rational rotor $\cosh\theta = 5/4$, $\sinh\theta = 3/4$ ($t = 4$): unit, fixing $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{4}$, scaling $I$ by $4$ and $\varphi$ by $1/4$, and carrying a frozen point along its hyperbola with $2ab$ preserved.

odd-extensions.twistor-algebra.technical:
For the ambient $\Cl(2,4)$ of the conformal completion, the even subalgebra satisfies $\Cl^0(2,4) \cong \Cl(2,3) \cong \Cl(4,1) \cong \Mat(4, \C)$, generated by the $e_ie_6$ for a spacelike $e_6$ or by the $e_ie_1$ for a timelike $e_1$. The volume element $\omega_6$ is even, central there, satisfies $\omega_6^2 = -1$, and is the complex unit. Inside it the $e_ie_6$ ($i = 2, \dots, 5$) generate a $\Cl(1,3)$ and the $e_ie_1$ a $\Cl(3,1)$, so both oriented shadows occur, and every input of the copy theorem lives in $\Cl^0(2,4)$ or its complexified modules.

Signature reversal does not identify the odd extensions: $\Cl(2,3) \not\cong \Cl(3,2)$ and $\Cl(1,4) \not\cong \Cl(4,1)$, because the centre is $\C$ for $\Cl(2,3)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$ but $\R \oplus \R$ for $\Cl(3,2)$ and $\Cl(1,4)$.
odd-extensions.twistor-algebra.lay: The algebra that acts on the four-component spinors of the conformal algebra turns out to be a five-dimensional Clifford algebra of signature (2,3), which is the same as four-by-four complex matrices. Both orientations of the spacetime algebra sit inside it, which is why the copy theorem cannot tell this world from its mirror. The odd-dimensional algebras one step up do tell the two orientations apart, because their centres differ.
odd-extensions.twistor-algebra.typing_note: The conformal-completion fact was added because the hypothesis and clause (iii) (twistor space as the module of the even subalgebra) rest on it; the copy-theorem fact was not added, since clause (iii) only lists that theorem's inputs and does not use its conclusion. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: (i) Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) applied to $\Cl(2,4)$ with a spacelike distinguished generator gives $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Cl(2,3)$, and with a timelike one $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Cl(4,1)$; both are $\Mat(4,\C)$ by Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. For $n = 6$ even, $\omega_{6}$ anticommutes with every vector, hence commutes with every even element, and $\omega_{6}^{2} = (-1)^{15}(-1)^{4} = -1$ (\claimref{std-algebra.pseudoscalar-commutation}, \claimref{primer.sign}); being even it lies in $\Cl^{0}(2,4)$ and is central there, and since $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Mat(4,\C)$ has centre $\C$, $\omega_{6}$ is the complex unit up to sign. (ii) The squares are $(e_{i}e_{6})^{2} = -e_{i}^{2}e_{6}^{2} = e_{i}^{2} = (1, -1, -1, -1)$ for $i = 2, \ldots, 5$ with the signature $(+,+,-,-,-,-)$, and $(e_{i}e_{1})^{2} = -e_{i}^{2} = (-1, 1, 1, 1)$; both sets anticommute pairwise and generate subalgebras of dimension sixteen. (iii) The conformal spin group is generated by the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$, which are even, and acts on $\CS$ through $\Cl^{0}(2,4)$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-conformal-completion}); the conformal spinor space $\CS \cong \C^{4}$ (twistor space) is the irreducible module of $\Cl^{0}(2,4) \cong \Mat(4,\C)$; the isotropic structure is a structure on $V_{\C} = \C^{6}$, the complexification of the ambient; and the mass formula is a bivector norm in the even subalgebra. (iv) An isomorphism of algebras restricts to an isomorphism of centres; the centre of an odd Clifford algebra is spanned by $1$ and $\omega$: a basis blade commutes with $e_{i}$ exactly when $e_{i}$ anticommutes with an even number of its factors, which for a blade of grade $k$ containing $e_{i}$ requires $k - 1$ even and for one not containing it requires $k$ even, and only the scalar and the volume element satisfy both conditions for every $i$; since $x \mapsto e_{i}xe_{i}^{-1}$ is diagonal in the blade basis, an element commutes with every $e_{i}$ exactly when each of its blades does, so the centre is spanned by those two (the script confirms dimension two over every odd signature of dimension at most five, and dimension one over every even signature of dimension at most six), and is $\R \oplus \R$ when $\omega^{2} = +1$ and $\C$ when $\omega^{2} = -1$; Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair} gives the signs. The script verifies (i), (ii) and the centre dimensions.

one-relation.imported-null-cone-determin.formal: For a real nondegenerate quadratic form $Q$ of mixed signature on $\R^{n}$, $n \geq 2$, the null cone $\{Q = 0\}$ determines $Q$ up to a nonzero real scalar: in an orthonormal basis $e_{1}, \dots, e_{p}, e_{p+1}, \dots, e_{n}$, a symmetric bilinear form $S$ vanishing on the null vectors $e_{i} \pm e_{j}$ ($i \leq p < j$) has $S(e_{i}, e_{j}) = 0$ and $S(e_{i}, e_{i}) = -S(e_{j}, e_{j}) =: a$ for all such pairs, and vanishing on $3e_{i} + 4e_{k} \pm 5e_{j}$ and $5e_{i} + 3e_{j} \pm 4e_{l}$ for distinct positive $i, k$ and distinct negative $j, l$ then kills the remaining off-diagonal entries, so $S = aQ$; at $n = 2$ the first family alone suffices. For $n \geq 3$ every bijection of Minkowski space preserving the causal order is generated by Lorentz transformations, translations and dilations, so causal structure and conformal structure coincide; in $n = 2$ the two null coordinates can be reparametrised independently and the causal automorphism group is infinite-dimensional. \emph{Provenance:} the first statement is the elementary computation displayed, which the script performs on every signature up to $(3,3)$, and is the statement that the null cone fixes the conformal class \cite{HawkingEllis1973}; the null-locus criterion, that $\Cl(p,q)$ contains a null vector if and only if $pq \neq 0$, is the root paper's \cite[Prop.~3.3]{ButlerT1}; the second statement is \cite{Zeeman1964}. All three enter Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts} as imports.
one-relation.imported-null-cone-determin.technical:
For a real nondegenerate quadratic form $Q$ of mixed signature on $\R^n$, $n \ge 2$, the null cone $\{Q = 0\}$ determines $Q$ up to a nonzero real scalar: a symmetric bilinear form vanishing on explicit null test vectors such as $e_i \pm e_j$ must equal $aQ$. The fact also records the series' null-locus criterion, that $\Cl(p,q)$ contains a null vector exactly when $pq \neq 0$.

For $n \ge 3$, Zeeman's theorem says every bijection of Minkowski space preserving the causal order is generated by Lorentz transformations, translations and dilations, so causal and conformal structure coincide; for $n = 2$ the two null coordinates can be reparametrised independently and the causal automorphism group is infinite-dimensional.
one-relation.imported-null-cone-determin.lay: Knowing which directions are light-like fixes the spacetime metric up to an overall scale. In three or more dimensions Zeeman showed more: any map of flat spacetime that preserves which events can influence which is built from rotations, boosts, shifts and rescalings. In two dimensions this fails, since each light direction can be stretched independently.

one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incid.formal: The complexified ascended algebra $\Cl(2,4)_{\C}$ acts irreducibly on the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ of a maximal isotropic $W \subset \C^{6}$, with the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor space) its even half; a nonzero conformal spinor $u$ has annihilator $W_{u} = \{v : c(v)u = 0\}$ of dimension exactly three, so every conformal spinor is the Fock vacuum of its own three-pair system, and $W_{u}$ determines $u$ up to scale. This is Cartan's purity theorem in the case $2\nu = 6$ (Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-cartans-purity-theorem-thouless-form}): every Weyl spinor of $\mathrm{Spin}(6, \C)$ is pure, the vacuum orbit being open in $\PCS = \mathbb{P}(\CS) = \mathbb{P}^{3}$ by the exceptional isomorphism $\mathrm{Spin}(6, \C) \cong SL(4, \C)$, which is the transitivity on which the twistor correspondence (of the conformal spinor space with spacetime) rests; it is a low-dimensional coincidence and not a generic property of Fock vacua, purity becoming one quadratic condition at $2\nu = 8$ (Remark \claimref{note.one-relation.where-exhaustiveness-first-fails-4-quadric}). A point of conformally compactified spacetime is a null vector of $\C^{6}$, equivalently a simple bivector of $\Lambda^{2}\CS$, that is, a line of the projective spinor space $\PCS$; the point embedding $X(x) = n_{0} + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)n_{\infty}$, with $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = 1$, is null identically, with the slot coefficient $-\tfrac12$ the only value for which it is, and the incidence relation is the completion's own chart. The completion's fibre quadric double covers the real slice of the Klein quadric. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1, Thm.~3.4, Thm.~4.2, Thm.~5.3]{ButlerT9}; \cite[Fact~2.3, Rem.~5.2]{ButlerT11}.
one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incid.technical:
The complexified $\Cl(2,4)_\C$ acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^\bullet W$ for a maximal isotropic $W \subset \C^6$, with the conformal spinor space $\CS$ the even half. Each nonzero conformal spinor $u$ has a three-dimensional annihilator $W_u$, is the Fock vacuum of its own three-pair system, and is fixed up to scale by $W_u$. This is Cartan's purity theorem at $2\nu = 6$, a low-dimensional coincidence: at $2\nu = 8$ purity becomes one quadratic condition.

A point of compactified spacetime is a null vector of $\C^6$, equivalently a simple bivector of $\Lambda^2\CS$, equivalently a line of $\PCS = \mathbb{P}(\CS)$. The point embedding $X(x) = n_0 + x - \tfrac12 Q(x)\,n_\infty$ with $\ip{n_0}{n_\infty} = 1$ is null identically, $-\tfrac12$ being the only slot coefficient for which it is, and the incidence relation is the completion's own chart; the completion's fibre quadric double covers the real slice of the Klein quadric.
one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incid.lay: This collects earlier results that the one-relation paper needs. In six complex dimensions every four-component spinor of the conformal algebra is the vacuum of its own small system of fermionic operators, a coincidence special to this dimension. Each point of spacetime corresponds to a line of such spinors, and the standard way of placing spacetime points into the six-dimensional space makes every point a light-like vector.

one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-l.formal:
Four clauses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Every point is null.)} Under the embedding of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}, $Q(X(x)) = 0$ identically: every point of spacetime is a non-invertible element of the algebra. Division by zero is not confined to special loci but is the condition of every point. The embedding needs $Q(x) = c^{2}t^{2} - |\mathbf{x}|^{2}$ dimensionally homogeneous, so the null embedding is where the third constant first enters the series (Lemma \claimref{one-relation.third-constant-conversion-constant-between-charts}).
\item \emph{(Every point is a projective line of vacua.)} The point's null vector acts on the Fock module of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart} as a nilpotent, $c(X(x))^{2} = Q(X(x)) = 0$, whose kernel has dimension four on the eight-dimensional module and exactly two on the conformal spinor half $\CS$ (twistor space): that two-dimensional kernel is the point's incidence line $L_{x}$. Every conformal spinor $u$ on $L_{x}$ is the Fock vacuum of its own three-pair system $W_{u}$, and $X(x) \in W_{u}$ for each of them: a point is not one vacuum but a projective line of distinct vacua, all of whose isotropic systems contain its null vector. Complexified compactified spacetime is the manifold of such lines, the Klein quadric of lines in $\PCS = \mathbb{P}(\CS)$, of which the real compactified spacetime is the real slice (double covered by the completion's fibre quadric, Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}); it is not the pure-spinor variety $\PCS$, which has one dimension fewer. Two points are null-separated exactly when their incidence lines share a vacuum: $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = -\tfrac12 Q(x - y)$.
\item \emph{(The location of each theory.)} The two theories then read: general relativity is the dynamics \emph{of} the vacua, how the vacuum family varies from point to point, carried by the connection; quantum mechanics is the dynamics \emph{above} a vacuum, excitations over a chosen vacuum obeying the CAR of Proposition \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations}. The choice of a vacuum on a point's incidence line is an extra datum, a null direction at the point, which the reading must supply and the point does not.
\item \emph{(Ubiquity, and what a singularity is.)} Quantum mechanics holds everywhere because every point carries its incidence line of vacua; a singularity is where the vacuum family degenerates, where the choice of vacuum itself becomes operator-valued, which is the sheaf paper's localisation theorem, in the Schwarzschild form the singularity paper carries, read in this language \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5, Thm.~8.12]{ButlerT4}, \cite[App.~B]{ButlerT5}.
\end{enumerate}
The series' statement is thereby sharpened: division by zero does not only mark special loci, it constitutes every point.
one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-l.technical:
Under the point embedding, $Q(X(x)) = 0$ for every $x$, so every point of spacetime is a non-invertible element of the algebra. On the Fock module $c(X(x))$ is nilpotent, with kernel of dimension four, two on the conformal spinor half: that kernel is the incidence line $L_x$, and each conformal spinor $u$ on it is the Fock vacuum of a three-pair system $W_u$ containing $X(x)$. So a point is a projective line of vacua, complexified compactified spacetime is the Klein quadric of such lines, and since $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = -\tfrac12 Q(x - y)$, two points are null-separated exactly when their lines share a vacuum.

Two further clauses are readings, not new dynamics: general relativity is the dynamics of the vacua, carried by the connection, and quantum mechanics the dynamics above a chosen vacuum, its CAR excitations, the choice of vacuum on a line being an extra null-direction datum; and a singularity is where the vacuum family degenerates, read through the sheaf localisation theorems.
one-relation.spacetime-manifold-vacuum-l.lay: In this picture every point of spacetime is a light-like vector, so in the algebra each point behaves like a zero divisor. Each point also carries a whole line of possible vacuum states, and two points are light-like separated exactly when their lines share a vacuum. The result then reads gravity as how these vacua change from point to point and quantum mechanics as the excitations above a chosen vacuum, with singularities where the family of vacua breaks down.

(1) is the nullity computation of Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart}. The script re-verifies it on the flat model with the inner product computed, not assumed: with $n_{0} = (e_{+} + e_{-})/2$, $n_{\infty} = e_{+} - e_{-}$ for $e_{\pm}^{2} = \pm 1$, it confirms $n_{0}^{2} = n_{\infty}^{2} = 0$, $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = 1$, then for six rational points with $Q(x)$ timelike, null and spacelike computes $Q(X(x)) = 0$ and $X(x)^{2} = 0$ in the algebra with $X(x) 
eq 0$, and confirms that any other slot coefficient $c$ gives $Q(X) = Q(x)(1 + 2c) 
eq 0$. A nonzero nilpotent is not invertible (\claimref{std-algebra.inverse-of-vector}: a vector is invertible exactly when $Q 
eq 0$). (2) By Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-pure-spinors-incidence-chart} a nonzero conformal spinor $u$ has $\dim W_{u} = 3$ and $W_{u}$ determines $[u]$; and $c(X)u = 0$ if and only if $X \in W_{u}$, by the definition of $W_{u}$. So the conformal spinors annihilated by $c(X(x))$ are exactly those whose isotropic system contains $X(x)$, and the set of such $[u]$ is the incidence line of the chart theorem, the line of $\mathbb{P}(\CS)$ that the simple bivector $X(x)$ represents. The kernel dimensions follow from nilpotency and the module structure: on the eight-dimensional Fock module a nonzero null vector has kernel of dimension exactly four, because the nonzero null vectors form a single $O(6,\C)$-orbit (Witt's extension theorem, Fact \claimref{one-relation.imported-witts-extension-theorem}), $c$ is equivariant under the Pin lift, so the rank of $c(X)$ is constant on the orbit, and at $X = w_{1}$ the operator is the wedge with one basis element of $W$, which annihilates exactly the four monomials containing it; and $c(X)$ swaps the chirality halves, so its kernel splits as two plus two. The script builds the Fock model explicitly (wedge and contraction on $\Lambda^{ ullet}W$, $\dim 8$, with the six ambient generators realised and all thirty-six anticommutators checked), and for each of the six points computes: $c(X)^{2} = 0$; kernel of dimension four, and two on each half; that two independent conformal spinors on the line and their sum each have a three-dimensional annihilator, pairwise distinct; that $X(x)$ lies in each of those annihilators; and, across the fifteen pairs of points, that the lines are pairwise distinct and meet exactly when the points are null-separated. The null-separation criterion in general: expanding with $n_{0}^{2} = n_{\infty}^{2} = 0$ and $\ip{n_{0}}{n_{\infty}} = 1$ gives $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = \ip{x}{y} - 	frac12 Q(x) - 	frac12 Q(y) = -	frac12 Q(x-y)$, which the script confirms on all fifteen pairs; and two incidence lines share a vacuum $u$ if and only if $X(x), X(y) \in W_{u}$ for some $u$, if and only if $X(x)$ and $X(y)$ span a totally isotropic plane (any two vectors of a maximal isotropic subspace are orthogonal; conversely an isotropic plane of $\C^{6}$ lies in exactly two maximal isotropic subspaces, which meet in it, so their intersection has odd codimension one in each and they lie in opposite families, exactly one of them the annihilator of a conformal spinor in $\CS$, which is also why two meeting incidence lines meet in one point), if and only if $\ip{X(x)}{X(y)} = 0$, since both are null. (3) and (4) are readings of (1)-(2) together with the imported theorems named (for (3) the CAR of \claimref{one-relation.two-presentations}; for (4) \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion} and \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport}, in the Schwarzschild form of \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion-singularity}), and are stated at that level: the content is the placement of the two theories on one object, not a new dynamical claim.

pairing.displacement-pairs-point-mode-va.technical:
On the flat model $W(x)$ is totally isotropic of dimension three, and the motion of the vacuum under a displacement $dx$ is generated by the translation bivector $\Omega(dx) = dx^a\, e_a n_\infty$, with $\tfrac12[e_a n_\infty, X(x)] = \partial_a X = e_a - x_a n_\infty$. pairing.imported-null-flags.lay: In relativity a single two-component spinor encodes a light-like direction together with a flag attached to it. Spinors taken up to scale correspond exactly to points of the sky, the celestial sphere. Rotating space by some angle turns the spinor by only half that angle.

pairing.stabiliser-parabolic-algebra-nul.formal:
Let $W = \operatorname{span}\{\ell, m\} \subset \C^{4}$ and define, on $\so(4,\C)$, the linear functional
\[
\pv(B) := \ip{B\cdot\ell}{m} .
\]
Then a bivector $B$ stabilises $W$ (that is, $B\cdot W \subseteq W$, which is the condition for the spin action of $B$ to fix the vacuum ray) if and only if $\pv(B) = 0$. On the basis, $\pv(e_{01}) = \pv(e_{23}) = 0$, $\pv(e_{02}) = 1$, $\pv(e_{03}) = i$, $\pv(e_{12}) = -1$, $\pv(e_{13}) = -i$; the stabiliser has complex dimension five, and its real points form the four-dimensional parabolic algebra of the null direction $\ell$,
\[
\mathfrak{p}(\ell) = \operatorname{span}_{\R}\{\,e_{01},\ e_{23},\ \ell e_{2},\ \ell e_{3}\,\},
\]
the boost in the plane of $\ell$, the rotation about its axis, and the two null rotations fixing $\ell$. The null rotations about $n$ move the vacuum: $\pv(n e_{2}) = 2$, $\pv(n e_{3}) = 2i$. The class of $B$ is the $\mb$-component of $B\cdot\ell$: $\pv(B) = 0$ exactly when $B\cdot\ell \in \operatorname{span}\{\ell, m\}$.
pairing.stabiliser-parabolic-algebra-nul.technical:
Let $W = \operatorname{span}\{\ell, m\} \subset \C^4$ and $\pi(B) = \ip{B \cdot \ell}{m}$ on $\so(4, \C)$. A bivector $B$ stabilises $W$, which is the condition for its spin action to fix the vacuum ray, exactly when $\pi(B) = 0$; equivalently, $\pi(B)$ is the $\bar m$-component of $B \cdot \ell$.

The stabiliser has complex dimension five, and its real points form the four-dimensional parabolic algebra $\mathfrak{p}(\ell) = \operatorname{span}_\R\{e_{01}, e_{23}, \ell e_2, \ell e_3\}$: the boost in the plane of $\ell$, the rotation about its axis, and the two null rotations fixing $\ell$. The null rotations about $n$ move the vacuum, with $\pi(n e_2) = 2$ and $\pi(n e_3) = 2i$.
pairing.stabiliser-parabolic-algebra-nul.lay: A vacuum here is labelled by a light-like direction. This result identifies exactly which Lorentz transformations leave it unchanged: a boost along that direction, a rotation about it, and two null rotations that keep the direction fixed. Every other transformation moves the vacuum, and a single number measures by how much.

proofs.main: $W$ is maximal isotropic, so $W^{\perp} = W$ and a vector $u$ lies in $W$ if and only if $\ip{u}{\ell} = \ip{u}{m} = 0$. For $B \in \so(4,\C)$ the action is skew, $\ip{B\cdot u}{v} = -\ip{u}{B\cdot v}$ (\claimref{std-algebra.bivector-lie-algebra}), so $\ip{B\cdot\ell}{\ell} = \ip{B\cdot m}{m} = 0$ automatically and $\ip{B\cdot m}{\ell} = -\pv(B)$. Hence $B\cdot\ell \in W$ and $B\cdot m \in W$ together reduce to the single condition $\pv(B) = 0$, and the stabiliser is the kernel of a nonzero functional on a six-dimensional space. The values on the basis are the commutators $\tfrac12[e_{ab}, \ell]$ paired with $m$; for instance $\tfrac12[e_{02}, e_{0} + e_{1}] = -e_{2}$ and $\ip{-e_{2}}{e_{2} + ie_{3}} = 1$. The four real elements listed have $\pv = 0$ (the null rotations because $\tfrac12[\ell e_{2}, \ell] = 0$, $\ell$ being null and anticommuting with $e_{2}$ (\claimref{std-algebra.orthogonal-anticommute})) and are linearly independent; the two real equations $\operatorname{Re}\pv = \operatorname{Im}\pv = 0$ are independent (the script checks the rank), so their real solutions form a space of dimension exactly four, which the four elements span. That the spin action of $B$ fixes the ray of the vacuum exactly when $B$ stabilises its annihilator $W$ is the definition of the annihilator, Fact \claimref{pairing.imported-two-readings-capacities-vacuum-null}. The script verifies every value, the equivalence ``$B\cdot W \subseteq W$ if and only if $\pv(B) = 0$'' on twenty random complex bivectors, the independence, and the two null rotations about $n$.

rungs.imported-spinor-identification-wit.formal: The complexified $\Cl(2,4)$ acts irreducibly on $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$. There is a canonical isomorphism $V_{\C} \cong \Lambda^{2}\CS$ of $\mathrm{Spin}$-modules under which the quadratic form is $P \mapsto \varepsilon(P \wedge P)$ for a fixed volume functional $\varepsilon$ on $\Lambda^{4}\CS$, and a vector is null exactly when its bivector is decomposable. In the incidence chart $\CS = \Som \oplus \Spi$ of the conformal spinor space (twistor space), a conformal spinor being $Z = (\omega, \pi)$, the lines of $\PCS = \mathbb{P}(\CS)$ skew to the line at infinity $L_{\infty} = \mathbb{P}(\Som)$ are the points of the chart, and the Witt pair $n_{0}, n_{\infty}$ of $V_{\C}$ consists of the bivectors of the two summands, $\Som \wedge \Spi$ being their common orthogonal complement. The real form of the ambient spin group is the conformal $SU(2,2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$, and a line of $\PCS$ is a point of the real conformal compactification exactly when it is null for the Hermitian form $\Sigma$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Rem.~3.2, Thms.~3.1, 3.4, 4.2, Props.~4.1, 4.5]{ButlerT9}.

standard-model.imported-fock-model-twist.formal: Let $V = \R^{2,4}$ be the ambient space of the conformal completion, $V_{\C} = W \oplus \overline{W}$ with $W$ a maximal isotropic subspace, $\dim W = 3$. The complexified algebra $\Cl(V_{\C}) \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$ acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, whose chirality halves are $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, the conformal spinor space and its opposite chirality (twistor space and its dual); there is a canonical isomorphism $V_{\C} \cong \Lambda^{2}\CS$ of $\mathrm{Spin}$-modules under which the quadratic form is $P \mapsto \varepsilon(P \wedge P)$ for a volume functional $\varepsilon$ on $\Lambda^{4}\CS$, and a vector is null exactly when its bivector is decomposable. In the chart $\CS = \Som \oplus \Spi$, $Z = (\omega^{A}, \pi_{A'})$, the bivector of $\Som$ is the point at infinity $n_{\infty}$. The opposite chirality is the conjugate of the conformal spinor space: the reality structure pairs $\CS$ with $\CSm$ and induces on $\CS$ the invariant Hermitian form (the twistor form) of signature $(2,2)$ preserved by $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4) \cong SU(2,2)$. The $\mathrm{Spin}$-invariant bilinear pairing of the module with itself is the top-degree pairing, pairing $\CS$ with $\CSm$ (degrees summing to three), twisted by the reversal sign on one argument. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~3.1, 3.4, Prop.~4.5]{ButlerT9}; proved there for three modes; the five-mode case is proved in Lemma \claimref{standard-model.invariant-pairing-five-modes} below.
standard-model.imported-fock-model-twist.technical:
For $V = \R^{2,4}$ with $V_\C = W \oplus \overline W$ and $\dim W = 3$, the algebra $\Cl(V_\C) \cong \mathrm{M}_8(\C)$ acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^\bullet W$, whose halves $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the conformal spinor space and its opposite chirality. There is a canonical $\mathrm{Spin}$-isomorphism $V_\C \cong \Lambda^2\CS$ with quadratic form $P \mapsto \varepsilon(P \wedge P)$, null vectors being decomposable, and in the chart $\CS = \Som \oplus \Spi$ the bivector of $\Som$ is $n_\infty$.

The reality structure pairs $\CS$ with $\CSm$ and induces on $\CS$ the invariant Hermitian form of signature $(2,2)$ preserved by $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4) \cong SU(2,2)$, and the invariant bilinear pairing of the module is the top-degree pairing of $\CS$ with $\CSm$, twisted by reversal on one argument.
standard-model.imported-fock-model-twist.lay: This restates how the four-dimensional spinor space of the conformal algebra arises inside the completed algebra of the series. The algebra acts on an eight-dimensional space built from three fermionic modes, which splits into two halves of opposite chirality. Vectors of the six-dimensional ambient space correspond to pairs of spinors from one half, and complex conjugation turns one half into the other, giving the Hermitian form whose symmetry group is the conformal group.

standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two.formal: Let $W$ be a maximal isotropic (three-dimensional) subspace of $V_{\C}$ with a dual isotropic complement. The complexified ascended algebra acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, and its two chirality halves are $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$, each of dimension four. Every nonzero conformal spinor (twistor) $u \in \CS$ is a pure spinor: it is the Fock vacuum of the system of three fermionic ladder pairs built on its own annihilator space $W_{u}$, every state of the module is generated from $u$ by those pair operators, and $\CS$ (respectively $\CSm$) is what the even (respectively odd) products generate. Conformal spinors are states of the pair algebra, not its operators. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~3.1]{ButlerT9} for the Fock model and the chirality halves; \cite[Thm.~5.3]{ButlerT9} for the pure-spinor and Fock-vacuum statements; the tower paper \cite[Thms.~4.2, 4.3]{ButlerT3} for the iterated pair structure (one qubit per rung, Witt index as capacity) within which this sits.
standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two.technical:
Let $W$ be a maximal isotropic, three-dimensional subspace of $V_\C$ with a dual isotropic complement. The complexified ascended algebra acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^\bullet W$, whose chirality halves $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ and $\CSm = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ each have dimension four. This is the chirality of the six-dimensional ascended algebra, the parity of the Fock grade; it is not the spacetime chirality at a point, whose two-dimensional halves $\Som$ and $\Spi$ split $\CS$ itself.

Every nonzero conformal spinor $u \in \CS$ is a pure spinor: it is the Fock vacuum of the three fermionic ladder pairs built on its annihilator $W_u$, every state of the module is generated from $u$ by those pair operators, and $\CS$ (respectively $\CSm$) is what the even (respectively odd) products generate. Conformal spinors are states of the pair algebra, not its operators.
standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two.lay: This restates earlier results of the series for the Standard Model paper. The completed algebra acts on an eight-dimensional space that splits into two halves of opposite chirality, four dimensions each (the chirality of the completed algebra, not the left and right handedness of spacetime spinors at a point). Every nonzero spinor in the first half is the empty state of its own three fermionic ladder pairs, and all other states are reached from it by those operators.

standard-model.imported-twistor-charge-h.formal: The charge read on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor charge), the homogeneity of the palatial quadratics, is helicity: the identification is the Penrose-transform homogeneity, whose offset is the ordering shift; the shift is proved in the twistor correspondence paper and the homogeneity $-2s-2$ is derived from it in the Hawking paper. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9}; \cite[Prop.~5.2]{ButlerT7}.
standard-model.imported-twistor-charge-h.technical:
The charge read on the conformal spinor space, the homogeneity measured by the palatial quadratics, is helicity. The identification goes through the Penrose-transform homogeneity $-2s-2$ for helicity $s$, whose offset of $-2$ is the symmetric-ordering shift.

The ordering shift is proved in the twistor correspondence paper, and the homogeneity $-2s-2$ is derived from it in the Hawking setting; the fact quotes both.
standard-model.imported-twistor-charge-h.lay: In Penrose's description the helicity of a massless particle, its spin along its direction of motion, shows up as the way a function on the spinor space of the conformal algebra scales. This fact records that the series' own charge on that space is exactly that scaling weight, with an extra shift of two coming from operator ordering. It is quoted from earlier papers of the series.

synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is.formal:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ with the conventions of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations}: $e_{0}^{2} = \nu^{2} = 1$, $e_{1}^{2} = e_{2}^{2} = e_{3}^{2} = e_{-}^{2} = -1$, $\nInf = \nu + e_{-}$, $\nO = \tfrac12(\nu - e_{-})$, $P_{a} = \tfrac12 a\nInf$ for $a \in \R^{1,3}$, $Z = e_{0}\nu$. Let $S$ be the module of three ladder pairs (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}) with its Hilbert form $\ip{\psi}{\phi}$, in which the frame generators squaring to $+1$ act self-adjointly and those squaring to $-1$ anti-self-adjointly, and $\CS$, $\CSm$ its two chirality halves. A bivector $B$ acts on $S$ by left multiplication, generating the rotor flow $\exp(tB)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The twistor form is the grading of $Z$.)} On $\CS$ (and on $\CSm$) the Hermitian forms invariant under all fifteen bivectors form a real line, spanned by $h(\psi, \phi) = \ip{\psi}{iZ\phi}$. It has signature $(2,2)$, and $Z$ acts as $-i$ on its positive plane $T_{+}$ and as $+i$ on its negative plane $T_{-}$. So the twistor form of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, an invariant Hermitian form on $\CS$, is a real multiple of $h$: the central rotation $Z$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-energy-selects-rule-2-sign}(i) is the grading that turns it into the Hilbert form, $h(\psi, iZ\phi) = \ip{\psi}{\phi}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Signs on the one-particle space.)} For a bivector $B$ put $q_{B}(\psi) = i\,h(\psi, B\psi)$, a Hermitian form. Then $q_{Z} = \ip{\psi}{\psi}$ is positive definite; for every future timelike or null $a$, $q_{P_{a}}$ and $q_{a\nO}$ are positive semidefinite, as is $q_{B}$ for the de Sitter horizon generator $B = P_{n} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}n\nO$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation} ($n$ future null, $\Lambda > 0$); for past $a$ they are negative semidefinite; for spacelike $a$, and for the boosts and the dilation, they are indefinite.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The oscillator model.)} Quantise $\CS$ with twistor operators $\hat Z^{\alpha}$, $[\hat Z^{\alpha}, \hat Z^{\beta\,*}] = (h^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}$, the components along $T_{+}$ annihilating ($a_{1}, a_{2}$) and those along $T_{-}$ creating ($b_{1}^{*}, b_{2}^{*}$), on the Fock space of four oscillators, and put $Q(M) = \sum_{\alpha\beta}\hat Z^{\alpha\,*}(hM)_{\alpha\beta}\hat Z^{\beta}$. Then $Q$ is a Lie homomorphism on $\so(2,4)$; the rotor flow $\exp(\tfrac{\tau}{2}Z)$, rotation through conformal time $\tau$, is generated by
\[
Q(\tfrac12 Z) = -iE, \qquad E = \tfrac12(N_{a} + N_{b}) + 1 ,
\]
and the Weyl-ordered central charge is $s = \tfrac12(N_{a} - N_{b})$. On the module of helicity $s$ the spectrum of $E$ is $|s| + 1 + n$, $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$, with multiplicity $(n + 1)(n + 2|s| + 1)$: the conformal energy of the twistor attachment, with the helicity of Proposition \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}. So that energy is the generator of the central rotation, and $E \ge 1$. In the other quantisation (components along $T_{+}$ creating, which quantises $-h$) the same flow has generator $-E$, bounded above. In the first quantisation $iQ(P_{a}) = \sum_{k}\lambda_{k}c_{k}^{*}c_{k} \ge 0$ for every future $a$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The series' modes meet the hypothesis.)} The oscillator representation integrates on each helicity module to a unitary representation of $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4) \cong SU(2,2)$ (cited) with $Z$ in its cone of nonnegative generators. The tower's CAR is the second quantisation over these modules (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}); second quantisation carries the representation to the Fock space with nonnegative generators preserved and the Fock vacuum invariant. So the Fock vacuum's GNS representation is a unitary representation of $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4)$ with nonnegative conformal energy and invariant GNS vector, the hypothesis of the stored positivity result, and by it every null translation of the flat background has a nonnegative generator fixing the vacuum.
\item[(v)] \emph{(What it gives for (N$_{+}$).)} Read on the light rays of a local Rindler horizon of Minkowski space (vanishing field strength), with the horizon modes the series' field on those rays (the reading of the adopted premise), the Fock vacuum is gauge-invariant (it commutes with the number charge), quasi-free, invariant under the affine null translations and a ground state for them: the attachment's vacuum satisfies the positivity and invariance clause of (N$_{+}$) in case (c), and no temperature, period or Euclidean section enters. The canonical light-ray component on which the modes are read is the one fixed on the null plane by clause (i) of the result filed alongside (synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group). With (ii) and the stored de Sitter result the same holds in case (b) for the conformally invariant fields of the attachment. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii) the state (N$_{+}$) admits is unique, so on these cases (N$_{+}$) says exactly that the state of the light rays is the attachment's vacuum restricted to them (in case (b), the conformal vacuum): a consistency result together with a restatement of the premise as the choice of that vacuum. The choice itself is not derived here. Case (a), the eternal hole, is not reached: its horizon translations are not background conformal transformations.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is.technical:
The stored positivity result reduces the ground-state premise (N$_{+}$) on the local horizons of Minkowski space to one hypothesis: the state's GNS space carries a unitary representation of the conformal spin group with nonnegative conformal energy, the generator of the central rotation $Z = e_{0}\nu$. The premise itself recorded that the series' modes were not shown to do so, and the rule-2 result called the identification of the twistor attachment's energy with $Z$ argued.

This claim closes that gap at the level of the twistor module. On the module of three ladder pairs the conformal spinors carry one invariant Hermitian form up to a real factor, and it is $\ip{\psi}{iZ\phi}$: the central rotation is exactly the grading that turns the indefinite twistor form into the positive Hilbert form. That single identity does the work. Quantising twistors in the usual way, the quadratic generated by $Z$ is the sum of the oscillator numbers plus one, $E = \tfrac12(N_{a} + N_{b}) + 1$, whose values on helicity $s$ are $|s| + 1 + n$ with the stored multiplicities. Every future translation, every null special conformal transformation and the de Sitter horizon's generator give positive semidefinite quadratics of the same sign, so in the quantisation that makes the conformal energy positive they are all nonnegative.

Second quantisation then gives a vacuum that is invariant and has nonnegative conformal energy, and the stored cone argument gives a ground state for every null translation. On the light rays of Minkowski local horizons this vacuum satisfies the condition (N$_{+}$) imposes in case (c), and with the stored de Sitter result in case (b) for conformal fields. Since the state the condition admits is unique, on those horizons (N$_{+}$) becomes the choice of the attachment's vacuum: the premise is restated, not removed. The eternal hole is not reached. The one-particle statements are checked exactly with Gaussian-rational matrices and polynomial oscillators; the integration to the group, the second-quantisation functor and the null-plane restriction are cited from memory.
synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is.lay: The series needs the quantum fields near a horizon to carry no negative energy along its light rays. An earlier result showed this follows if the fields have nonnegative energy for one special symmetry, a rotation that mixes time with an extra direction of the series' enlarged algebra. Whether the series' own fields have that property had been left open. They do. The twistors from which the series builds its fields carry a quantity that can be positive or negative, and that special rotation is exactly what converts it into an ordinary positive length. Quantised, the rotation's energy comes out as the energies already stored for the fields, all positive, and every push along a light ray costs nonnegative energy too. So the vacuum of the series' fields satisfies the no-negative-energy condition on horizons in empty space, and on the horizon of an expanding universe for the fields that ignore rescaling, without assuming any temperature. That the fields are actually in that vacuum is still an assumption: the condition becomes the choice of this one state. Black holes are still not covered.

proofs.main:
The module. Realise the six generators on $S = \C^{8}$, the Fock space of three ladder pairs of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.twistors-are-states-three-ladder-pairs}, by the Jordan-Wigner matrices $g_{1} = \sigma_{x}\otimes 1\otimes 1$, $g_{2} = \sigma_{y}\otimes 1\otimes 1$, $g_{3} = \sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{x}\otimes 1$, $g_{4} = \sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{y}\otimes 1$, $g_{5} = \sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{x}$, $g_{6} = \sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{y}$ (Hermitian, squares $1$, pairwise anticommuting), with $e_{0} = g_{1}$, $\nu = g_{2}$, $e_{1} = ig_{3}$, $e_{2} = ig_{4}$, $e_{3} = ig_{5}$, $e_{-} = ig_{6}$. The check verifies the Clifford relations of the stated signature, that the volume element is $i$ times the chirality $\sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{z}\otimes\sigma_{z}$, that every bivector commutes with the chirality, so $\CS$ and $\CSm$ (its two eigenspaces, the even and odd states of the pair system) are invariant and four-dimensional, and that $Z^{2} = -1$. The Hilbert form is the standard one on $\C^{8}$, and generators squaring to $\pm 1$ are Hermitian, respectively anti-Hermitian, as stated. Any other realisation of the module is unitarily equivalent to this one on each chirality half, so the statements below do not depend on the choice.

\emph{(i)} A sesquilinear form $\ip{\psi}{X\phi}$ is invariant under the rotor flow of $B$ exactly when $B^{*}X + XB = 0$. For $X = iZ$ this holds for all fifteen bivectors (computed); $iZ$ is Hermitian. Writing the fifteen conditions on $\CS$ as a linear system for the sixteen entries of a $4\times 4$ matrix $X$, exact elimination over the Gaussian rationals gives a kernel of complex dimension one, so every invariant sesquilinear form is a complex multiple of $h = \ip{\cdot}{iZ\,\cdot}$ and every invariant Hermitian form a real multiple. The same holds on $\CSm$. On $\CS$, in the Jordan-Wigner basis, $iZ = \mathrm{diag}(-1, -1, 1, 1)$ and $Z = \mathrm{diag}(i, i, -i, -i)$: signature $(2,2)$, $Z = -i$ on $T_{+}$ and $+i$ on $T_{-}$; $Z$ is the generator of the centre of the maximal compact subalgebra of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-energy-selects-rule-2-sign}(i), whose identification with the attachment's energy that result left argued. The twistor form of the attachment is an invariant nondegenerate Hermitian form on $\CS$, hence a nonzero real multiple $c\,h$, and $h(\psi, iZ\phi) = \ip{\psi}{(iZ)^{2}\phi} = \ip{\psi}{\phi}$ since $(iZ)^{2} = -Z^{2} = 1$.

\emph{(ii)} $q_{B}(\psi) = i\ip{\psi}{iZB\psi}$ has matrix $i\,hB$ on $\CS$, Hermitian for every bivector $B$ by (i). For $B = Z$, $hZ = iZ\cdot Z = -i$, so $q_{Z} = \ip{\psi}{\psi}$. For the other generators the check computes $i\,hB$ exactly and tests all fifteen principal minors: positive semidefinite for $P_{a}$ with $a = e_{0}$, $e_{0} \pm e_{1}$, $e_{0} + \tfrac35 e_{2} + \tfrac45 e_{3}$, $e_{0} + e_{3}$ (null and timelike future vectors) and $2e_{0} + e_{1}$, $5e_{0} + 3e_{1} + 4e_{3}$ (timelike); the same for $a\nO$ and for $P_{a} + \tfrac{\Lambda}{12}a\nO$ at $\Lambda = 3, \tfrac37, 12$, which for null $a = n$ is the de Sitter generator $\tfrac12 nI$; negative semidefinite for the past vectors $-a$; indefinite for the spacelike $a = e_{1}$, $e_{2}$, $e_{0} + 2e_{1}$, and for the boost $e_{0}e_{1}$, the dilation $\nu e_{-}$ and the boost $e_{1}e_{-}$. For general future $a$ the statement follows from these by the structure of the cone: $a \mapsto q_{P_{a}}$ is linear, and the future cone is generated by future null vectors, all positive multiples of $e_{0} + \hat n$ with $\hat n$ a unit spatial vector, and so conjugate to $e_{0} + e_{1}$ up to positive scale under the spatial rotations, which commute with $Z$, while $q$ transforms by congruence under those rotations (they preserve $h$ and commute with $Z$), so semidefiniteness and its sign are preserved; $a\nO$ is handled the same way.

\emph{(iii)} With $T_{-}$ spanned by the first two basis vectors and $T_{+}$ by the last two, set $\hat Z^{\alpha} = b_{\alpha}^{*}$ on $T_{-}$ and $\hat Z^{\alpha} = a_{\alpha}$ on $T_{+}$; then $[\hat Z^{\alpha}, \hat Z^{\alpha\,*}] = -1$, resp. $+1$, which is $(h^{-1})^{\alpha\alpha}$. The check realises the four oscillators on polynomials (creation as multiplication, annihilation as differentiation, exact). From $[\hat Z^{\alpha\,*}, \hat Z^{\gamma}] = -(h^{-1})^{\gamma\alpha}$ one gets $[Q(M), \hat Z^{\gamma}] = -(M\hat Z)^{\gamma}$, hence $[Q(M), Q(N)] = Q([M, N])$ for the bivector generators; the check confirms the homomorphism exactly on three pairs and two test states. Since $hZ = -i$, $Q(\tfrac12 Z) = -\tfrac{i}{2}\sum_{\alpha}\hat Z^{\alpha\,*}\hat Z^{\alpha} = -\tfrac{i}{2}(b_{1}b_{1}^{*} + b_{2}b_{2}^{*} + a_{1}^{*}a_{1} + a_{2}^{*}a_{2}) = -\tfrac{i}{2}(N_{a} + N_{b} + 2) = -iE$; the check confirms this on all $625$ monomials of degree at most $4$ in each oscillator. The trace of $\tfrac12 Z$ on $\CS$ vanishes, so this ordering agrees with the Weyl ordering and no constant is free. The centre of $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$, $M = \tfrac{i}{2}\,\id$, has Weyl-ordered quadratic $\tfrac{i}{2}\cdot\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha}h_{\alpha\alpha}(\hat Z^{\alpha\,*}\hat Z^{\alpha} + \hat Z^{\alpha}\hat Z^{\alpha\,*}) = \tfrac{i}{2}(N_{a} - N_{b}) = is$ (checked). On helicity $s \ge 0$ the states have $N_{a} = N_{b} + 2s$, so $E = N_{b} + s + 1 = |s| + 1 + n$ with $n = N_{b}$, and the number of monomials is $(N_{a} + 1)(N_{b} + 1) = (n + 2|s| + 1)(n + 1)$; symmetrically for $s < 0$. The check tabulates every $(s, E)$ with $|s| \le 2$ and $n + 2|s| \le 4$. These are the energies and multiplicities of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, and the charge $s$ is the distinguished $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge of Proposition \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}, up to the orientation of that charge, which the energies do not see since they depend on $|s|$. In the other quantisation the commutators are $[\hat Z^{\alpha}, \hat Z^{\beta\,*}] = -(h^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}$, so it quantises $-h$; there $Q(\tfrac12 Z) = +iE$ (checked on three monomials), a generator bounded above. For future $a$, write the positive semidefinite $i\,hP_{a} = \sum_{k}\lambda_{k}v_{k}v_{k}^{*}$ with $\lambda_{k} \ge 0$; then $iQ(P_{a}) = \sum_{k}\lambda_{k}c_{k}^{*}c_{k}$, $c_{k} = \sum_{\beta}\overline{(v_{k})_{\beta}}\hat Z^{\beta}$, a sum of positive operators. The check confirms nonnegative Fock expectation values for four future null translations on five test states, a strictly positive value on some, and a negative value for the past translations; on the lowest state of the module ($E = 1$, $s = 0$) the expectation of $iQ(P_{e_{0} + e_{1}})$ is $1$.

\emph{(iv)} The oscillator representation of $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$ on each helicity module integrates to a unitary irreducible representation of $SU(2,2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4)$, the ladder representations (Mack and Todorov; Mack; cited from memory); its generator $iQ(\tfrac12 Z) = E$ is bounded below by $1$, so $\tfrac12 Z$, and hence $Z$, lies in the cone $C_{\pi}$ of nonnegative generators in the sense of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-gives-positive-null-translations}. Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} states that the tower's CAR is the second quantisation over this positive-energy one-particle space (via the Penrose transform, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-standard-field-theory}). The second-quantisation functor sends a unitary $U$ to $\Gamma(U)$ on Fock space, fixes the vacuum, and sends a nonnegative generator $A$ to $d\Gamma(A) \ge 0$ (cited from memory, standard); so the Fock vacuum's GNS representation carries a unitary representation of $\mathrm{Spin}^{+}(2,4)$ with $Z \in C_{\pi}$ and invariant GNS vector. By the stored positivity result every future translation, in particular every null translation along the generators of a local Rindler horizon of the flat background, has a nonnegative generator, and the vacuum is invariant under it.

\emph{(v)} The Fock vacuum is quasi-free (its correlations are those of the one-particle projection) and gauge-invariant (the number charge annihilates it). Its restriction to the field on the light rays of a null plane of Minkowski space is then a gauge-invariant quasi-free state invariant under the null translations of the plane, with nonnegative generator: the clause of Premise (N$_{+}$) in case (c), read with the horizon modes the series' field on those rays: its canonical component on the null plane $N_{k}$ is $\Lambda(m)\psi$, $m$ the dual null vector, by clause (i) of the result filed alongside (synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group), on which the restriction is the continuum mode space of each generator (the light-ray algebra of a free massless field, cited from memory, Wall; Casini, Teste and Torroba). No temperature, period or Euclidean section enters. For the de Sitter field, (ii) gives the same sign for $\tfrac12 nI$, which together with Proposition \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation}(iii) to (v) gives the clause in case (b) for the conformally invariant fields of the attachment. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii) a state satisfying the clause on a generator is unique (the filled sea), so on these cases the clause is equivalent to the statement that the state of the light rays is the attachment's vacuum restricted to them (in case (b), the conformal vacuum). This shows that the vacuum satisfies the clause and restates (N$_{+}$) there as the choice of that vacuum; it does not derive the choice. For case (a) the stored de Sitter result shows that the Schwarzschild field admits no gauge in which its horizon translations are background conformal transformations, so nothing here reaches it. $\square$

synthesis.imported-twistor-equation-inte.formal: Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric is smooth, and read its Weyl curvature $\mathcal{W}$ in two-spinor form as the Weyl spinor $\Psi_{ABCD}$ (a reading, as in Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). The twistor equation for a spinor field $\omega^{A}$ is $\nabla_{A'}^{(A}\omega^{B)} = 0$; its integrability condition is $\Psi_{ABCD}\,\omega^{D} = 0$. Hence at every point where a nonzero solution exists, either $\Psi_{ABCD} = 0$ (Petrov type O) or $\Psi_{ABCD} = \Psi_{4}\,o_{A}o_{B}o_{C}o_{D}$ with $\omega$ proportional to $o$ (Petrov type N, $\omega$ the fourfold repeated principal spinor): the twistor equation restricts the field to Petrov type N or O. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Ch.~6]{PenroseRindler1986}; \cite{GasperinPais2024}.
synthesis.imported-twistor-equation-inte.technical: Twistors on a curved background are the solutions of the twistor equation, and they exist in full number only where the Weyl curvature vanishes. The obstruction is the integrability condition, the Weyl spinor contracted with the twistor's primary part, which must vanish. A nonzero spinor annihilated by the Weyl spinor is a principal spinor of multiplicity four, so at any point where a nonzero solution exists the Weyl curvature is of Petrov type N, with that spinor as its repeated principal spinor, or vanishes (type O). This is standard twistor theory (Penrose; Penrose and Rindler, vol. 2), stated, for example, by Gasperin and Pais.
synthesis.imported-twistor-equation-inte.lay: Twistors, the objects from which the series builds its quantum states, can be carried consistently through a gravitational field only where a certain part of the field, the part that describes tidal stretching and gravitational waves, is either absent or of the special form of a pure gravitational wave. This standard result of twistor theory is taken from the literature.

synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-give.technical:
The series' boundary modes attach to spacetime through the conformal spinor space, whose one-particle spaces are positive-energy representations of the conformal group: the conformal energy is bounded below. The ascent to $\Cl(2,4)$ singles out one generator for that energy, the rotation $Z = e_{0}\nu$ of the plane of the two directions that square like time, which spans the centre of the maximal compact subalgebra. This result shows, by exact identities in $\Cl(2,4)$, that positivity of $Z$ in a unitary representation forces positivity of every future translation. Among these are the null translations along the generators of the local Rindler horizons of Minkowski space.

Conjugating $Z$ by the dilation and rescaling, the remainder $\rho^{-4}e_{0}\nO$ dies and the time translation $P_{e_{0}}$ is left. Conjugating that by a boost and rescaling leaves the null translation $P_{\ell}$. The generators with nonnegative spectrum in a unitary representation form a closed convex cone invariant under conjugation, so they contain every future translation once they contain $Z$. Spacelike translations are conjugate to their negatives and cannot lie in such a cone unless they act trivially. This is the standard equivalence of positive conformal energy and the spectrum condition (Segal; Mack 1977; L\"uscher and Mack 1975), proved here in the conformal model; it is transport-absent apart from its $\Cl(2,4)$ form.

The representation must act on the space where the state lives: for a field, the GNS (filled-sea) Fock space, on which the second-quantised generators are nonnegative when the one-particle ones are. It does not act on a one-particle space such as $L^{2}(\R, du)$ of a generator, where the null momentum takes both signs. For the vacuum of such a field the result supplies the positivity half of the ground-state condition used by the result filed alongside, synthesis.positive-null-energy-gives-r-premises. With it, (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) holds on the local Rindler horizons of Minkowski space in the continuum restatement given there. Its scope is flat spacetime with vanishing gravitational field. The result filed alongside, synthesis.de-sitter-horizon-translation-is-conformal-null-rotation, extends the positivity half to the cosmological horizons of the de Sitter gravitational field, a pure dilation of the flat background, for conformally invariant fields. For the Schwarzschild field, whose field strength is pure nonzero Weyl, the positivity of the affine null translations is part of the premise. For a gravitational field of nonvanishing field strength the local form of (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) needs the state to be, at leading order near the point, invariant under the local null translations, which is a condition on the state.

Remark (argued). The twistor attachment (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}) has conformal energies $|s| + 1 + n > 0$. That this energy is generated by $Z$ is the standard identification, which the stored rule-2 result argues and does not prove. That the series' boundary modes carry such a representation on their state's GNS space is likewise argued, not proved. Granting both, the attachment's fields satisfy the spectrum condition. They would then meet the hypotheses of the Bisognano-Wichmann theorem of Fact \claimref{angle.imported-theorems-deliver-their-hypotheses} if they are Wightman fields (temperedness, locality, finite-component fields), which is not shown here.
synthesis.positive-conformal-energy-give.lay: The series' quantum fields are built so that a particular kind of energy, the energy that goes with the symmetries of light cones, is never negative. This result shows, by exact algebra, that this one requirement forces the ordinary energy, and the momentum along every light ray of flat spacetime, to be non-negative too. It is a known result, here written in the series' own algebra. It matters for the temperature of horizons. A companion result shows that if the momentum along a horizon's light rays is non-negative and the fields are in their lowest-energy state, an observer on one side of the horizon sees them as thermal at exactly the right temperature. Put together, the small horizons of flat spacetime get their temperature from positivity of energy. On its own this result does not reach the horizons of black holes. A companion result shows that, for massless fields of the kind unchanged by rescaling distances, it does reach the horizon of a universe driven by a cosmological constant: in the series' language spacetime is flat everywhere, that universe's gravitational field only rescales lengths, and sliding along its horizon's light rays is one of the symmetries of light cones. A black hole's gravitational field also stretches and squeezes by different amounts in different directions, a tidal effect no change of description removes. That the series' modes carry this kind of energy is argued, not proved.

synthesis.quartic-ordering-tensor-locall.technical:
Suppose the deformed palatial product keeps the reordering defects of symmetrised quadratics inside the quadratics, so that the quartic ordering tensor is a deformed Lie bracket on the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$. That bracket is rigid: the second cohomology of $\mathfrak{sl}(4)$ with adjoint coefficients vanishes, which the check computes exactly from the Chevalley-Eilenberg complex at torus weight zero (dimensions $3, 21, 87, 273$, ranks $3, 18, 69$). So every such deformation is undone by redefining which elements count as the generators $q(M)$, and the tensor carries no invariant data at a point.

It can still carry googly-shaped data as a redefinition. A spin-two map of the self-dual factor, extended by zero, gives a first-order deformation whose defects vanish on anti-self-dual and mixed Lorentz words and are nonzero, in the googly slot, on self-dual words (it also changes brackets with the non-Lorentz generators, but never those of the anti-self-dual factor): it passes the anti-self-dual consistency check and has the five components of a self-dual Weyl spinor. Under the closure hypothesis, then, the conjecture's part (b) can hold only globally, as the failure of local redefinitions to patch, much as anti-self-dual data lives in the patching of curved twistor space.
synthesis.quartic-ordering-tensor-locall.lay: A long-standing problem in twistor theory is where the "right-handed" half of gravitational curvature can be stored. The series conjectures that it sits in a specific place: in how the order of multiplying certain quantum operators matters at fourth order. This result tests that idea in the case where the reordering of those operators stays among the same kind of operators. In that case the relevant algebra is rigid: any small change of it can be undone by relabelling which operators are called the basic ones. So, assuming that closure, the right-handed curvature cannot be stored at any single point in a way that relabelling cannot remove. It can, however, appear there in exactly the right shape and without disturbing the left-handed half, which the result exhibits. So the conjecture survives only in a global form: the information would have to sit in how local relabellings fail to fit together, which is how twistor theory already stores the left-handed half.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} Write $C^{k} = \operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda^{k}\mathfrak{s}, \mathfrak{s})$ with the Chevalley-Eilenberg differential $(dc)(x_{0}, \dots, x_{k}) = \sum_{a}(-1)^{a}[x_{a}, c(\dots\hat{x}_{a}\dots)] + \sum_{a<b}(-1)^{a+b}c([x_{a}, x_{b}], \dots\hat{x}_{a}\dots\hat{x}_{b}\dots)$, where $\mathfrak{s} = \mathfrak{sl}(4,\C) \cong \mathfrak{sl}(\CS)$ by Proposition \claimref{correspondence.spin-representation}. The Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$ acts on $C^{k}$ by the Lie derivative $L_{H}$, which commutes with $d$ and satisfies $L_{H} = d\,\iota_{H} + \iota_{H}\,d$ (Cartan's formula, with $(\iota_{H}c)(x_{1}, \dots) = c(H, x_{1}, \dots)$). On the subcomplex of torus weight $\lambda \neq 0$ choose $H$ with $\lambda(H) \neq 0$; for a cocycle $c$ there, $c = \lambda(H)^{-1}L_{H}c = d(\lambda(H)^{-1}\iota_{H}c)$, so that subcomplex is acyclic and $H^{k}(\mathfrak{s}, \mathfrak{s})$ is the cohomology of the weight-zero subcomplex, the cochains mapping each tuple of basis vectors into the weight space of the sum of their weights. In the basis $E_{ij}$ ($i \neq j$), $H_{k} = E_{kk} - E_{k+1,k+1}$, the weight-zero cochain spaces in degrees $0, 1, 2, 3$ have dimensions $3, 21, 87, 273$ and the check computes the ranks of $d_{0}, d_{1}, d_{2}$ exactly as $3, 18, 69$, with $d_{2}d_{1} = 0$; so $\dim H^{1} = 21 - 18 - 3 = 0$ and $\dim H^{2} = 87 - 69 - 18 = 0$. (This is Whitehead's second lemma for $\mathfrak{sl}(4)$, recomputed.) Rigidity follows by the standard order-by-order argument (Gerstenhaber's deformation theory, cited from memory for attribution): if $\mu \equiv [\,,\,]$ modulo $\hbar^{m}$ after a redefinition, the Jacobi identity for $\mu$ at order $\hbar^{m}$ says that $\mu_{m}$ is a 2-cocycle, hence $\mu_{m} = d\phi_{m}$, and conjugating by $1 - \hbar^{m}\phi_{m}$ (with the sign fixed by $d$) removes it modulo $\hbar^{m+1}$; the product of these maps is $\Phi$. Then with $Q = q\circ\Phi^{-1}$, $Q(X)\star Q(Y) - Q(Y)\star Q(X) = \hbar\,q(\mu(\Phi^{-1}X, \Phi^{-1}Y)) = \hbar\,q(\Phi^{-1}[X, Y]) = \hbar\,Q([X,Y])$, the undeformed relation of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.symmetrised-quadratics-palatial-algebra}(2). The ordering tensor of Lemma \claimref{correspondence.ordering-filtration}(2) is, under (CQ), $\mu$ read through $q$; so its class modulo redefinitions of the generators is zero.

\emph{(ii)} By Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}(1) one of $\mathfrak{g}^{\pm}$ acts faithfully on $\Som$ and trivially on $\Spi$, the other the reverse, so in a basis of $\CS$ adapted to $\Som \oplus \Spi$ they are the two diagonal $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ blocks, and $[\mathfrak{g}^{+}, \mathfrak{g}^{-}] = 0$ as in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}(1); which block is called self-dual does not matter below. With $(h_{+}, e_{+}, f_{+})$ the standard basis of $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$, the map $\phi(f_{+}) = e_{+}$, $\phi = 0$ on $h_{+}, e_{+}$, on $\mathfrak{g}^{-}$ and on the rest of $\mathfrak{s}$, satisfies $[\operatorname{ad}h_{+}, \phi] = 4\phi$ on $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\phi(x)y) = \operatorname{tr}(x\phi(y))$ on $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$: it is the highest-weight vector of the spin-two summand of $\operatorname{End}\mathfrak{g}^{+} \cong \mathfrak{g}^{+}\otimes\mathfrak{g}^{+} = \mathbf{1}\oplus\mathbf{3}\oplus\mathbf{5}$ (the symmetric traceless part; complete reducibility as in Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-complete-reducibility} is not needed beyond this explicit vector). For $M, N \in \mathfrak{g}^{-}$, $\phi M = \phi N = \phi[M,N] = 0$, so $d\phi(M,N) = 0$; for $M \in \mathfrak{g}^{-}$, $N \in \mathfrak{g}^{+}$, $d\phi(M,N) = [M, \phi N] = 0$ since $\phi N \in \mathfrak{g}^{+}$ commutes with $M$, and $[N, \phi M] = \phi[M,N] = 0$. On $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$, $d\phi(h_{+}, f_{+}) = [h_{+}, e_{+}] - [f_{+}, 0] - \phi(-2f_{+}) = 4e_{+} \neq 0$, and all values on $(\mathfrak{g}^{+}, \mathfrak{g}^{+})$ lie in $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$. For $M \in \mathfrak{g}^{-}$ and $Y \in \mathfrak{p}$, $d\phi(M, Y) = [M, \phi Y] - [Y, \phi M] - \phi[M, Y] = 0$, because $\phi Y = \phi M = 0$ and $[\mathfrak{g}^{-}, \mathfrak{p}] \subset \mathfrak{p}$, on which $\phi$ vanishes. For $N \in \mathfrak{g}^{+}$ and $Y \in \mathfrak{p}$, $d\phi(N, Y) = -[Y, \phi N] - \phi[N, Y]$, and for $Y, Y' \in \mathfrak{p}$, $d\phi(Y, Y') = -\phi[Y, Y']$, nonzero whenever $[Y, Y']$ has an $f_{+}$ component; the check exhibits nonzero values on both. So $\phi$ is supported on $\mathfrak{g}^{+}$ but $d\phi$ is not: the redefinition changes brackets with the non-Lorentz generators too, which the anti-self-dual consistency check does not see. Under $\mu = [\,,\,] + \hbar\,d\phi$, the defects of words in $q(\mathfrak{g}^{-})$ are those of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.chirality-split-ordering-insensitivity-asd-sector}(2)(a), and the googly slot still commutes with $q(\mathfrak{g}^{-})$ to first order, so the consistency check is passed; the check verifies all of this exactly, together with $(1 + t\phi)([M,N] + t\,d\phi(M,N)) - [(1 + t\phi)M, (1 + t\phi)N] = t^{2}(\phi\,d\phi(M,N) - [\phi M, \phi N])$ at $t = \tfrac17$, which exhibits $d\phi$ as the first-order transport of the bracket by $1 + \hbar\phi$. A spin-two tensor of the self-dual factor has the five components of a self-dual Weyl spinor; that this is the right identification is a reading, not proved here.

\emph{(iii)} By (i), under (CQ) a deformation defined over an open set of the spacetime (or of the twistor data) is, on each small patch $U$ where the order-by-order construction runs, the redefinition $\Phi_{U}$. Invariant content therefore resides only in the transition data $\Phi_{U}^{-1}\Phi_{V}$, which is argued, not proved, to be where part (b) would have to locate the googly data, by analogy with the nonlinear graviton, whose anti-self-dual data is the patching of a locally standard twistor space (Fact \claimref{correspondence.imported-nonlinear-graviton} records the construction; it is not used in the proof). Deformations in which $q(M)\star q(N) - q(N)\star q(M)$ leaves the span of the quadratics, as a deformation of the full palatial algebra generally may, are outside (CQ) and untouched by this argument.
